result.summary: I audited per-learner bulk-issue outcomes (A4), revocation and its audit trail (A7) and the audit log generally, against private copies of the app on ports 5200-5207 (all stopped). A4 and A7 hold: I could not produce a wrong outcome, a duplicate or missing audit event, a partial write or a cross-tenant effect, including under concurrency across two server processes, external lock holders, injected write failures and a SIGKILL mid-operation. The four findings are peripheral: a verification test that does not test the savepoint it claims to guard, a revoke dialog that says "was not revoked" when the outcome is unknown, and two nits.
checksPerformed: Setup: copied the deliverable to /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/61a877e9-483e-575a-b7cf-c5b8e94decb9/scratchpad/audit2/outcomes-revocation-audit/app and read README.md plus the backend services, schema, seed, generator, app.js, the bulk-issue and detail UI components, and the A4/A7 tests. Scripts are in the sibling scripts/ directory (lib.py, a4.py, fuzz.py, ui1-3.cjs).
Author's suite: ran the three backend test files in my copy (TMPDIR pointed at my scratch dir): 105 tests, 105 pass, about 29 s. This matches the README claim.

A4, every seeded course in both tenants (a4.py): predicted each learner's outcome from the SQLite file, then compared with the roster preview and the real bulk issue for courses 1-6. All matched: Safety 101 East and West 2 issued / 3 skipped, First Aid 1/4 (Mei Chen certificate_revoked), Working at Heights 1/3 (Grace Kim certificate_revoked), Forklift and Manual Handling 0 issued. Summary counts equalled the per-learner list; every skip had a reason and message.

A4, database effects of each issue: certificate row correct (tenant, course, learner, enrollment, snapshot names, bulk_operation_id, status active), serial prefix EAST-/WEST- and consecutive, exactly one certificate.issued event with correct actor, tenant, operation id and created_at equal to issued_at. Deltas of certificates, audit events and last_serial equalled the issued count. A second run with a new key issued 0. GET /api/bulk-issues/:id returned the POST body byte for byte.

Roster preview vs real operation: paged GET /api/courses/:id/enrollments with pageSize 1, 2, 3, 7 and 100 and compared with the unpaged roster, totals, summary.eligible and the real outcomes for every learner. This ran on the seed data, inside the 3,900-step fuzz, and on a generated 10,000-learner course (100 pages, 10,000 distinct learners, ordered by name then id, totals 9,807 certified / 193 revoked equal to the DB, preview equal to the result for all 10,000). Roster parameter validation (page 0, x, repeated, pageSize 101, limit and per_page aliases) and 404s for foreign, unknown and malformed course ids were correct.

Forced issuance failures: (a) blank learner name, so the certificates CHECK fails on the first write; (b) a trigger aborting the audit insert, so the failure comes after the serial reservation and certificate insert; (c) a trigger raising RAISE(ROLLBACK). In (a) and (b) the learner was reported failed, the others were issued, no certificate or audit row remained for the failed learner, last_serial was not consumed, counts matched, the replay returned the stored failure and a new key retried only that learner. In (c) the request answered 500, nothing was written, the key was not burned and the server stayed healthy.

Crash safety: on a course with 60,005 enrollments I SIGKILLed the server 350 ms into the bulk issue. No certificate, audit event, operation or serial advance remained and integrity_check was ok. After restart the same key executed once (54,002 issued, 54,002 audit events) and then replayed identically. That operation blocked the process for about 2.8 s; the README lists background jobs for very large bulk issues as out of scope, so I did not report it.

Bulk-issue input edge cases: courseId as a numeric string, 2.0 and 2e0 accepted; "02", true, arrays, objects, unsafe integers, wrong key case, top-level array/string/number, empty body and concatenated JSON all gave 400 with no operation row. An empty course gave 201 with total 0. Foreign and unknown courses gave 404 with nothing written.

A7, basic revocation: a valid revoke returned 200 with alreadyRevoked false, status revoked, revokedAt/revokedBy/trimmed reason, and exactly one certificate.revoked event whose created_at equals revoked_at. Six repeats (no body, empty body, {}, another reason, reason null, extra fields) returned alreadyRevoked true, left the row unchanged and added no event.

A7, invalid input and ids: non-string reason, 501 characters, control characters, lone surrogate, array body, malformed JSON, top-level string/number/null, form-encoded, bad gzip and utf-16 charset all gave 400; a 200 kB body gave 413; none wrote anything. Ids 0, -1, abc, 1e3, 3.0, 03, padded, 16 and 40 digits, unknown and other-tenant all gave 404; a missing or unknown actor gave 401; GET, PUT and DELETE gave 404.

A7, concurrency: 60 simultaneous revokes of one certificate split over two server processes on one database file (East and West) gave exactly one alreadyRevoked false, 59 true, one audit event and identical revokedAt and reason in every response. With a third connection holding BEGIN IMMEDIATE, 20 revokes on both servers queued while reads and an already-revoked repeat were answered in 1-2 ms, then produced one event after release. With DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS=1500 and the lock held, the revoke answered 503 with Retry-After after 1.5 s and wrote nothing; the retry revoked once.
A7, atomicity: with a trigger aborting the certificate.revoked audit insert, the revoke answered 500 and the certificate stayed active; after dropping the trigger it revoked once.

After revocation: the list shows revoked and the status filters agree with the DB; the detail shows revokedAt, revokedLocal, revokedBy, the reason and both audit events; the export follows the status filter (3 active, 7 revoked, 10 all); a later bulk issue skips with certificate_revoked; a replay of the original operation still returns its stored result, as documented.

Audit invariant fuzz (fuzz.py, seeds 1-3, 3,900 steps, two servers on one file, invariants re-checked after every step): random bulk issues (with and without key, 1-10 concurrent identical requests, alternative body shapes), replays, 409 conflicts, unreadable bodies, cross-tenant and invalid requests, revokes (active with 1-8 concurrent, already revoked, foreign, unknown, invalid) and external writes adding learners and enrollments or flipping completion, including duplicate and awkward names. Invariants: one issued event per certificate and one revoked event per revoked certificate with correct tenant, actor, timestamp and operation id; none on active certificates; no orphans; event total equals certificates plus revoked; last_serial equals the highest serial; operation counts equal stored bodies, certificates and events; rejected, replayed and no-op requests change nothing. Result: 0 problems.

Mixed concurrent stress: 12 s of 6 bulk-issue threads, 6 revoke threads and an external writer against both servers (7,050 bulk requests, 6,092 revokes, 450 external transactions) gave no non-2xx answers and all invariants held. No certificate was issued for a non-completed enrollment and no serial was duplicated.

100,000-row dataset: ran the generator against a live database. Every generated certificate has exactly one issued event and every generated revoked one exactly one revoked event. A bulk issue on a generated course skipped all 10,000 with 0 audit events. After --clear there were no orphan audit events or operations and foreign_key_check was clean.

GET /api/audit-events: tenant scoping (another tenant's certificateId or bulkOperationId returns 0), newest-first order equal to the DB, paging with pageSize 3 over 6 pages with no gaps, filters certificateId, bulkOperationId and action alone and combined, the limit and operationId aliases. Invalid page, pageSize and id values and repeated parameters gave 400. See the nit about unknown action values and the 9-digit limit.

Operation history: GET /api/bulk-issues is tenant-scoped, newest first, capped at 10, with summaries equal to the stored operations. GET /api/bulk-issues/:id returns 404 for other-tenant, unknown and malformed ids.

Actor attribution: a mixed-case, padded X-Actor-Email is recorded as the canonical email. With a second East admin inserted, concurrent same-key requests from both admins ran as separate operations, and certificates, audit events, issuedBy and revokedBy named the admin who actually acted.
db:reset under two running servers: afterwards a4.py passed again with the pristine predictions, so the servers keep working on the re-seeded data.

UI with Playwright on a build in my copy: the detail drawer shows serial, learner, course, tenant-local issue date, status and audit trail. Revoke opens a confirmation; Cancel and Escape send nothing and Escape closes only the confirmation. A double-click on confirm sent one POST; afterwards the status, audit trail and list row update and the revoke button disappears. A certificate revoked elsewhere while the drawer was open gives the 'already revoked; nothing was changed' message. A foreign deep link shows 'Certificate not found'.

UI bulk issue: the preview matched the result, a double-click on Issue sent one POST with one Idempotency-Key, and a failed learner is shown with the Failed tile, filter and note. 'View outcomes' on a 60,005-learner operation rendered in about 0.2 s (first 200 rows) and the roster paginated over 1,201 pages.

Test sensitivity by mutation in a separate copy (app-mut): removing the per-learner savepoint left all 93 unit and acceptance tests green (finding 1). Removing the status = 'active' guard from the revoke UPDATE is caught, but only by the two-server lock test; the A7 test named 'concurrent revocations still produce a single audit event' passes without the guard because a single process handles the 12 requests serially.

Considered and not reported: a revoked certificate is never re-issued (skip reason certificate_revoked). The README documents this and it does not contradict the spec wording 'completed, not yet certified'. A roster page on a 10,000-learner course costs about 35 ms regardless of page size, which is structural but small.
Cleanup: every server I started (ports 5200-5207) was stopped by its recorded PID; nothing was created or run inside /home/user/cert-admin-console.

findings.title: The 'leaves no partial writes' test passes with the per-learner savepoint removed
findings.location: backend/test/acceptance.test.js:811-875 (hook at 827, assertions at 844-864); guarded code at backend/src/services/bulkIssue.js:157-170
findings.description:
The README credits the A4 mechanism 'Each learner is issued inside a savepoint, so one failure becomes a failed outcome without undoing the others' to the test 'simulated failure'. That test injects the failure through hooks.beforeIssue, which runs before issueCertificate has written anything (bulkIssue.js:159). At that point there is no serial reservation, certificate row or audit row to undo, so the assertions 'leaves no partial writes' and 'did not consume a serial number either' hold whether or not the savepoint exists.

I removed the savepoint entirely and all 93 unit and acceptance tests still passed. The same mutant, in real use, leaves a certificate with no audit event for a learner it reports as failed. The shipped code is correct here (I verified it with a trigger that fails the audit insert); the gap is that a regression would go unnoticed.
findings.expected: The test that claims to guard against partial writes should fail when the savepoint is removed, i.e. inject the failure after at least one write of the learner's unit of work.
findings.reproduction:
1. Copy backend/ to a scratch directory and, in src/services/bulkIssue.js, replace `const certificate = db.transaction(() => {` ... `});` (lines 157-170) with an immediately invoked function `(() => { ... })()`, so there is no SAVEPOINT.
2. Run `node --test --test-concurrency=1 test/unit.test.js test/acceptance.test.js`. Observed: tests 93, pass 93, fail 0, including 'A4 - a failing learner does not take the others down'.
3. Start the mutant on a fresh database and create `create trigger t_fail before insert on audit_events when NEW.action='certificate.issued' and NEW.details like '%Emily Davis%' begin select raise(ABORT,'audit store unavailable'); end`.
4. As bob@west.test, POST /api/bulk-issues {"courseId":4}. Observed on the mutant: Emily Davis 'failed', yet certificate id 12 'WEST-0000005' exists for her with 0 audit events, and Jordan Smith gets WEST-0000006.
5. Same steps on the unmodified code: no certificate for Emily, Jordan gets WEST-0000005, last_serial 5.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a hook that runs after the certificate insert (or make the audit insert fail, as the trigger above does) and assert that no certificate row, no audit row and no serial increment remain for the failed learner.

findings.title: Revoke dialog says 'The certificate was not revoked' when the response was lost but the server did revoke it
findings.description:
Every error from the revoke request is shown as 'The certificate was not revoked: <message>'. For a network failure (ApiError status 0) the outcome is unknown: the server may already have revoked the certificate and written the audit event.

In that case the dialog makes a false statement about an irreversible action. The drawer keeps showing 'Active' with the Revoke button, and the list is not refreshed because onChanged is only called on success. If the admin cancels, the console shows an active certificate that is in fact revoked until the page is reloaded.

The bulk-issue page handles the same situation correctly ('may or may not have gone through', 'Retry safely'). Server-side the retry is idempotent, so no data is harmed; the defect is the wrong statement and the stale state.
findings.expected: For errors with an unknown outcome (network failure, timeout) the dialog should say that the revocation may or may not have been applied, and the detail and list should be reloaded.
findings.reproduction:
Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/61a877e9-483e-575a-b7cf-c5b8e94decb9/scratchpad/audit2/outcomes-revocation-audit/scripts/ui2.cjs (Playwright, built UI on port 5205).
1. Open #/certificates/6 as alice@east.test, click 'Revoke certificate…', then confirm, with a route handler that forwards the POST to the server and then aborts the response (`await route.fetch(); return route.abort();`).
2. Observed in the dialog: 'The certificate was not revoked: The server could not be reached. Check that it is running, then try again.' The drawer status still reads Active.
3. Observed in the database at that moment: certificate 6 has status 'revoked', revoked_at 2026-11-23T12:32:47.910Z, and audit event 17 'certificate.revoked'.
4. Clicking 'Try again' with the network restored shows 'This certificate had already been revoked; nothing was changed.', which confirms the first attempt had taken effect.
findings.suggestedFix: In RevokeDialog, branch on error.retryable or status 0: word it as 'may or may not have been revoked; retrying is safe', and on such errors call detail.reload() and onChanged() so the drawer and list show the server's state.

findings.title: Failed outcome message passes the raw SQLite error to API clients and the UI
findings.location: backend/src/services/bulkIssue.js:50-53 and 184; backend/src/db/schema.js (learners.full_name has no non-blank CHECK, certificates.learner_name does)
findings.description:
failureMessage() copies err.message into the per-learner result, so the stored response, every replay and the UI results table show database internals such as 'CHECK constraint failed: length(trim(learner_name)) > 0'.

The trigger I used is a learner whose name is blank. The schema allows that in learners but refuses it in certificates. The roster preview marks such a learner 'Will be issued', and every bulk issue then fails for them with this message, so the learner stays 'eligible' indefinitely. Isolation itself is correct: the other learners are issued and nothing partial remains.
findings.expected: A failed outcome should carry a message an admin can act on (for example 'learner has no name'), with the raw driver error kept in the server log.
findings.reproduction:
1. On a fresh database run `update learners set full_name='   ' where id=3` (East, Marcus O'Connor).
2. GET /api/courses/1/enrollments as alice@east.test: that learner has eligible true and summary.eligible is 2.
3. POST /api/bulk-issues {"courseId":1}: 201, summary {total 5, issued 1, skipped 3, failed 1}; the failed result has message 'Certificate could not be issued: CHECK constraint failed: length(trim(learner_name)) > 0'.
4. The UI results table shows the same text (screenshot /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/61a877e9-483e-575a-b7cf-c5b8e94decb9/scratchpad/audit2/outcomes-revocation-audit/shots/bulk-failed.png).
5. A new key fails the same learner again; the roster still reports eligible 1.
findings.suggestedFix: Map known constraint failures to plain messages and fall back to a generic one, logging the original error; optionally classify a blank-named learner as not issuable in classifyEnrollment so preview and result agree.

findings.title: GET /api/audit-events ignores unknown action values and rejects ids above 9 digits with a misleading message
findings.description:
Two small validation inconsistencies in the audit filters.

- An unknown action value is not rejected: ?action=bogus and ?action=CERTIFICATE.REVOKED return 200 with total 0. A mistyped filter therefore looks like 'no audit events', whereas the certificate list rejects an unknown status with 400.
- certificateId and bulkOperationId declare max 1e15, but queryInteger only accepts 1-9 digits. ?certificateId=1234567890 is answered 400 'must be a whole number' although it is one, while path ids accept up to 15 digits and ?certificateId=0 reports the range 'between 1 and 1000000000000000'.

Neither is reachable with realistic data volumes.
findings.expected: Unknown action values should give 400 listing the two valid actions; the id filters should accept the range they announce, or announce the range they accept.
findings.reproduction:
With X-Actor-Email: alice@east.test on a seeded database:
- GET /api/audit-events?action=bogus -> 200, total 0, items [].
- GET /api/audit-events?action=CERTIFICATE.REVOKED -> 200, total 0.
- GET /api/audit-events?certificateId=1234567890 -> 400 'Query parameter "certificateId" must be a whole number'.
- GET /api/audit-events?certificateId=0 -> 400 '... must be between 1 and 1000000000000000'.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate action against AUDIT_ACTIONS, and either widen the digit pattern in queryInteger to match max or lower max to 999999999.

result.summary: I audited A6 and the generator CLI on a private copy and found no acceptance-criterion failure: every export I checked was correct, deterministic, complete and far inside the 60 s limit, and the generator, db:reset and write-lock behaviour work as the README describes. The defects are all limited: a filtered export with few matches blocks the server for its whole scan (20–110 ms at 100,000 rows, about 265 ms at 250,000), exports have no concurrency cap or idle timeout (60 concurrent took RSS from 65 MB to 1.3 GB and it stayed above 1 GB), the generator permanently advances East's serial counter, and search is case-insensitive only for ASCII. All processes I started are stopped and the original tree was not touched.
checksPerformed: Generator, documented command (`npm run generate:east` on a freshly seeded copy): Python sqlite3 dump before/after shows exactly 100,000 certificates added, all for East, West unchanged at 4; every quick-start row in admins, courses, learners, enrollments, certificates and audit_events is byte-identical. The only changed seed row is tenants East last_serial 7 -> 100007 (reported). integrity_check ok, foreign_key_check empty.

Generated data shape: 2,466 distinct learner names (max 110 duplicates), 13 course titles (10,000 each for generated ones), 4,007 distinct issue instants (25 per batch), 669 local dates (up to 400 per day), status 98,066 active / 1,941 revoked. Serial numbers are unique by schema, so that column cannot have duplicates.

Generated data consistency: issued_local_date equals an independent zoneinfo Australia/Sydney conversion for all 100,007 East rows (42,406 of them have a local date different from the UTC date); every generated certificate has exactly one issued audit event and every revoked one exactly one revoked event.

Generator options: --count 1, 7, 10, 11, 1e3, 100000 and 250000 (8.9 s) all work; re-run replaces the previous set (count stays 100,000, content identical apart from serials); --seed 42 gives different data; --clear and a second --clear restore the seed rows (except last_serial); --db with a new nested path creates and seeds the file; --tenant West / east (case-insensitive) work; --help works.

Generator bad input: --count 0, abc, 1.5, empty, 2000001, --seed x and unknown tenant give a clean message, exit 1 and no data change. --count -5, an unknown flag, a positional argument, a directory or a non-SQLite file as --db exit 1 with a raw Node stack trace (reported as nit).

Generator and reset races on a scratch DB: two generators at once, generator plus db:reset, reset plus generator all end in a valid state (integrity ok, 0 FK violations). Export correctness at 100,007 rows: 76 filter/sort combinations (all 5 sort keys x asc/desc, unfiltered, q=an + status=active, q=EAST-00 + status=revoked, plus 23 search strings including %, _, backslash, quote, comma, apostrophe, non-ASCII, padded). Each was run twice: bytes identical, header equals 'Learner Name,Course Title,Serial Number,Issue Date (Australia/Sydney)', and rows plus exact order equal an independent Python computation (zoneinfo local date, sort key, id tie-breaker). 0 failures; slowest export 0.34 s.
Larger volume: at 250,007 rows a full sorted export took 0.8–1.2 s and a filtered one 0.5 s, byte-identical on repeat.

CSV quoting and LIKE escaping on a scratch DB with 26 hand-inserted learner names (commas, quotes, LF, CRLF, tabs, formula triggers, %, _, backslash, emoji, full-width, case variants of 'Alex Lee') and a course title with comma, quotes and newline: Python csv round-trips every cell exactly (apart from the README-documented apostrophe prefix on formula cells); q=%, _, \\ match only rows containing those literal characters; names equal under NOCASE are ordered by id.

Export parameter validation: bad sort/order/status, repeated q, q longer than 100 characters and a NUL byte give 400 JSON; a missing actor gives 401; POST gives 404; HTTP/1.0 (non-chunked) export is byte-identical to the chunked one.

List vs export page by page: for 14 sort/filter combinations I walked every page (pageSize 100, up to 1,001 pages). The concatenated list rows equal the CSV rows and the independent ordering, no id is repeated or skipped, and the reported total is constant and equals the rows returned.

Event-loop stall per export (polling /api/health): about 11 ms for a full export, but equal to the whole export duration for selective filters (reported).

Exports started during a generator run: 10 spaced and 60 dense (every 70 ms) exports were all 200, complete, and equal either to the full pre-generator state or the full post-generator state, never a mix or a truncation.

Afterwards every table is identical to the pristine seed dump (including tenants.last_serial and all ids; only SQLite's internal sqlite_stat tables are extra), the file shrank from 80 MB to 176 KB, and the server kept serving list, detail, courses, audit, bulk issue and revoke.
Exports started during db:reset: 10 spaced and 60 dense exports were all 200 and complete, each equal to the full 100k pre-reset state or the 7-row post-reset state.

Stalled export across maintenance: across one db:reset, and separately across 3 generator runs plus a --clear, the resumed download was complete, properly terminated and equal to its original snapshot (after-effects on WAL size and the next write are reported).

Write lock held by another process (Python BEGIN IMMEDIATE): held 4 s, revoke and bulk issue waited about 3.5 s and returned 200/201; held 13 s, both returned 503 with Retry-After: 1 after 10.0 s with nothing written (row counts unchanged), and the retries then succeeded. Meanwhile export, detail, re-revoke of an already revoked certificate, replay of a finished bulk issue (1 ms, identical body) and key misuse (409 in 1 ms) were answered without waiting; health max 12–52 ms.

UI via Playwright on 100k rows: the Export CSV download is byte-identical to the API export for the default view (100,008 rows, 0.4 s), for search 'zhou' + status revoked + learner A-Z, for text typed and exported before the 300 ms debounce (the table then shows the same filter), and after a header-click sort; a real double-click sends one export; the list re-sorted in 73 ms while an export was running; 'Last' goes to page 4,001 of 4,001 with 8 rows.

Deliverable's own scale suite (backend/test/scale.test.js) run in my copy: 12/12 pass in 19.5 s. Its responsiveness test uses only unfiltered exports and a 2,000 ms threshold (noted in the first finding).
Bulk issue on a generated 10,000-learner course: 201 in 101 ms (2.3 MB response), replay in 19 ms; not reported because the README lists large bulk issues as out of scope.

findings.title: A filtered export with few matching rows blocks the event loop for its whole table scan
findings.description:
The export yields to the event loop after every 500 rows that SQLite returns, not after every 500 rows it scans. With a selective search or status filter, a single rows.next() call walks the entire tenant index (plus a table lookup per row to evaluate LIKE on the other column) before returning. The whole export, including the first batch computed before the 200 is sent, is then one synchronous block, and every other request waits for it.

Measured at 100,007 East rows, the longest /api/health and list wait equals the export duration:
- q=alex, sort=learner: 60 ms (112 ms on the node:sqlite driver)
- q=alex, sort=course: 44 ms
- q=alex, sort=issued: 34 ms
- q=zzz-nomatch, sort=learner: time to first byte 80–116 ms
- full unfiltered export, for comparison: 11 ms

The stall grows with tenant size: at 250,007 rows (the documented `--count 250000`) the same q=alex, sort=learner export blocked the server for 265 ms.

Under load the fairness the design promises disappears. Four clients looping selective exports pushed list latency from a 2 ms median to a 426 ms median (max 541 ms) and /api/health to a 203 ms median. By contrast, 24 concurrent full exports only raised the list median to 36 ms.

This contradicts README section 7: "control returns to the event loop after each batch — a concurrent request waits for at most one batch (well under a millisecond of work)". A6 is worded for a filtered export. At the specified 100,000 rows the block is at most about 0.1 s per export, so I rate it minor rather than an A6 failure.

The verification suite cannot see it: the test 'list requests stay responsive while exports are streaming at full speed' uses only unfiltered exports (`export.csv?sort=learner|course|issued`) and asserts worst < 2,000 ms.
findings.expected: Spec section 3.4 / A6: a filtered and sorted export must "not block concurrent certificate list API requests during export". README section 7: a concurrent request waits for at most one batch, well under a millisecond.
findings.location: backend/src/services/certificates.js:354-369 (batch loop counts returned rows; rows.next() scans unboundedly); backend/src/app.js:135 (first batch pulled synchronously before responding); backend/test/scale.test.js:222-249 (test uses unfiltered exports, 2 s threshold)
findings.reproduction:
1. In a private copy: `npm run generate:east`, then `PORT=5300 LOG_REQUESTS=0 node backend/src/server.js`.
2. Run a Node script that polls GET /api/health and GET /api/certificates?page=1&pageSize=25 in tight keep-alive loops while issuing one GET /api/certificates/export.csv?q=alex&sort=learner&order=asc with X-Actor-Email: alice@east.test (median of 5 runs).

Observed: 'q=alex sort=learner (1 row matches): export 61 ms (120 bytes) | longest /api/health wait during export: 60 ms | longest list wait 62 ms | idle baseline max health 2 ms'. Same script, full export sort=learner: export 719 ms, longest health wait 11 ms. At --count 250000: export 264 ms, longest health wait 265 ms, longest list wait 261 ms.

3. Four concurrent loops of export.csv?q=zzz-nomatch&sort=learner and export.csv?q=Alex%20Lee&sort=course for 6 s: list n=15 med=426.5 ms max=541.2 ms; health med=203.2 ms. Baseline: list med=2.2 ms, health med=0.1 ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Bound the work per event-loop turn by rows scanned, not rows matched. For example, walk the ordering index in key-range chunks (keyset: WHERE (sort_key, id) > (:k, :id) LIMIT n on the unfiltered index, applying the search predicate per chunk), or run the export query in a worker thread. Add a scale test that measures list/health latency during an export whose filter matches 0–1 rows, with a threshold in the tens of milliseconds.

findings.title: No cap on concurrent exports: each costs about 20 MB that is not returned, plus a retained file descriptor
findings.description:
Every export opens its own SQLite connection, and better-sqlite3's default page cache is 16 MB per connection (PRAGMA cache_size = -16000). A full 100k export fills that cache, so process memory grows by roughly 20 MB per concurrent export. There is no limit on concurrent exports.

Measured on a freshly started server:
- RSS 65 MB at start, 98 MB after one export, 130 MB after 20 sequential exports.
- 1,300 MB after 60 concurrent exports. It was unchanged 3 s later, did not grow on a second round of 60 (so it is a plateau at peak concurrency, not a per-request leak), and was still 1,089 MB several minutes and many requests later.
- An earlier process went from 123 MB to 546 MB after 24 concurrent exports and plateaued there.

File descriptors follow the same pattern: 25 before, 85 after 60 concurrent exports, with 61 fds on cert-admin.sqlite while only one connection is open. SQLite cannot close an fd while another connection in the process holds a lock on the same file, so it parks them for reuse.

README section 7 says "Memory use is flat". That holds per export in the JS heap, but not for the process.
findings.expected: README section 7: "Memory use is flat." Spec section 3.4: 100,000-row exports must be handled efficiently.
findings.location: backend/src/app.js:124-131 (new reader connection per request, no concurrency limit); backend/src/db/sqlite.js:314-321 (reader opened with the driver's default 16 MB cache)
findings.reproduction:
PID=<server pid>; grep VmRSS /proc/$PID/status -> 64824 kB; ls /proc/$PID/fd | wc -l -> 25.

for i in $(seq 1 60); do curl -s -o /dev/null -H 'X-Actor-Email: alice@east.test' 'localhost:5300/api/certificates/export.csv?sort=course' & done; wait

Afterwards: VmRSS 1300160 kB, fds=85 (61 of them on cert-admin.sqlite). 3 s later: unchanged. After another 60: 1303108 kB, fds=85. Minutes later: VmRSS 1089164 kB.

`node -e` with better-sqlite3 on a copy of the DB: PRAGMA cache_size -> -16000.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a small cache on reader connections (for example PRAGMA cache_size = -1024; the export is a sequential index walk), and/or serve exports from a small bounded pool of reader connections with a queue or a 429 beyond the limit.

findings.title: A stalled export download is never timed out and pins its snapshot across maintenance runs
findings.description:
A client that stops reading keeps its read transaction and connection open indefinitely; there is no idle or write timeout on the export response. Reads and writes are not blocked during the stall and the download stays a correct snapshot (both verified). The after-effects are:

- **WAL growth.** The WAL cannot be checkpointed past the pinned snapshot. With one stalled export open, three generator runs and one --clear grew cert-admin.sqlite-wal from 81 MB to 312 MB.
- **Event-loop stall on the next write.** The first write the server commits after the stalled download finishes runs the deferred checkpoint synchronously inside COMMIT. A single revoke took 591 ms and /api/health was blocked for 585 ms; the next write still took 164 ms. For comparison, the first write after a generator run with no stalled export stalled 38 ms, and 143 ms when ordinary exports were streaming during the generator's commit.
- **db:reset does not shrink the files.** With a stalled export open, `npm run db:reset` printed 'Demo data restored' and exited 0, but the database stayed 80.4 MB with a 77 MB WAL. The script swallows the busy checkpoint. The main file only shrank (to 176 KB) on a later server write, and the WAL stayed at 77 MB, then 16 MB.

README sections 4 and 9 state without qualification that db:reset shrinks the file and that a write lock held elsewhere no longer blocks the server.
findings.expected: README section 4: "`npm run db:reset` removes it and shrinks the database file back to its original size". README section 7: a request handler never freezes every other request of the process.
findings.location: backend/src/app.js:124-152 (no timeout on the export stream); backend/scripts/init-db.js:51-59 (checkpoint failure swallowed); backend/src/db/sqlite.js:272 (COMMIT runs the auto-checkpoint on the request thread)
findings.reproduction:
1. Server on :5300 with 100k rows. A Python raw socket with SO_RCVBUF=4096 sends GET /api/certificates/export.csv?sort=issued&order=asc, reads 20 KB, then stops reading.
2. Run `npm run generate:east` twice, `npm run generate:east -- --clear`, `npm run generate:east`. WAL size after each: 80,883,872 / 161,767,712 / 230,785,952 / 311,673,912 bytes.
3. Resume the download: 100,007 rows, equal to the original snapshot.
4. Node script polling /api/health while sending POST /api/certificates/6/revoke: 'revoke 6: status 200 in 591 ms; longest /api/health during: 585 ms'. Next: 'revoke 7: status 200 in 164 ms; longest /api/health during: 164 ms'.
5. Separately: stalled export, then `npm run db:reset` -> exit 0, 'Demo data restored', but sizes {db: 80449536, wal: 77208832}; list total is 7.
findings.suggestedFix: Give the export response an idle timeout (destroy the stream if no bytes were accepted for N seconds), which releases the snapshot. Have db:reset report when it could not shrink the files. Optionally run large checkpoints outside the request path.

findings.title: The generator permanently advances East's serial counter, and --clear does not restore it
findings.description:
The spec asks for a generator that works "without altering the default quick-start dataset". Every other quick-start row is untouched (verified row by row), but the seeded tenants row for East is modified: last_serial goes from 7 to 100007 on the first run and advances by `count` on every further run. `--clear` leaves it there.

- After three 100k runs and a --clear, the database is back to 7 East certificates but last_serial = 301036. In my working database it reached 700010 after seven runs.
- The quick-start demo then behaves differently from the README: a Safety 101 bulk issue issued Priya Sharma EAST-0700010, where README section 5 shows "serialNumber": "EAST-0000008".
- Only `npm run db:reset` brings the counter back.

The README documents the choice ("only East's serial-number counter advances"), and the test's quick-start snapshot deliberately omits last_serial, so this is a documented interpretation that conflicts with the spec wording.

Two related inaccuracies:
- README section 4 says "every run produces the same rows". Learner, course, status and dates are identical between runs, but serial numbers are not.
- Serials are zero-padded to 7 digits and sorted as text. Once the counter passes 9,999,999 (100 default runs, or 5 runs at --count 2000000), sort=serial is no longer numeric. I reproduced this only by setting last_serial = 9999990 directly and generating 30 rows: the order became EAST-0000007, EAST-10000000, ...
findings.expected: Spec section 2: "Provide a separate CLI command or script to generate 100,000 certificate rows for one tenant (`East`) without altering the default quick-start dataset."
findings.location: backend/src/db/generate.js:141 (reserveSerials inside generateCertificates); backend/src/db/generate.js:74-92 (deleteGenerated / clear do not reset tenants.last_serial); backend/src/services/ledger.js:13-15 (7-digit padding); backend/test/scale.test.js:41 (snapshot omits last_serial)
findings.reproduction:
cp seed.sqlite g1.sqlite; node backend/scripts/generate-certificates.js --db g1.sqlite --count 100000 (three times, the last with --seed 42); node backend/scripts/generate-certificates.js --db g1.sqlite --clear.

Python comparison against the pristine dump: all tables identical except tenants: [1,'East','EAST','Australia/Sydney',7,...] -> [1,'East','EAST','Australia/Sydney',301036,...].

On the server database after seven generator runs: GET /api/certificates?q=priya&sort=serial -> ('EAST-0700010', 'Safety 101').

Signature of generated rows in id order: with serials 58506aa0a9f1 vs 98d7c74a473b on a re-run; without serials 476c3170cd15 both times.
findings.suggestedFix: Give generated certificates a serial range that does not consume the tenant counter (for example a distinct prefix such as EAST-LT-0000001), or restore last_serial on --clear and on re-run when no non-generated certificate was issued in between. Then include last_serial in the test's quick-start snapshot.

findings.title: Search is case-insensitive only for ASCII: 'álvarez' and 'JOSÉ' do not find the seeded learner 'José Álvarez'
findings.criterion: Spec section 3.1 / 3.4 (search by learner name; export preserves search)
findings.description:
The search filter uses SQLite LIKE, which folds case only for ASCII letters. Search is therefore case-insensitive for 'lee' / 'LEE' but case-sensitive for any non-ASCII letter.

On the quick-start data, which contains the learner 'José Álvarez':
- q=josé, q=José, q=Álvarez, q=ÁLVAREZ -> 1 result
- q=JOSÉ, q=álvarez -> 0 results

The same filter drives the CSV export, so an export for 'álvarez' is empty. An admin typing a name in lower case, which works for every other learner, silently gets no rows for this one. This is slightly outside my assigned area; I hit it while testing export filters.
findings.expected: Search by learner name should behave consistently; since it is case-insensitive for ASCII names, the seeded non-ASCII name should be found regardless of case.
findings.reproduction:
Fresh quick-start data, header X-Actor-Email: alice@east.test:
- GET /api/certificates?q=%C3%A1lvarez -> total=0
- GET /api/certificates?q=%C3%81lvarez -> total=1 ['José Álvarez']
- GET /api/certificates?q=%C3%81LVAREZ -> total=1
- GET /api/certificates?q=JOS%C3%89 -> total=0
- GET /api/certificates?q=jos%C3%A9 -> total=1
- GET /api/certificates/export.csv?q=%C3%A1lvarez -> header line only (70 bytes)
findings.suggestedFix: Store a normalised search column (for example a Unicode-lower-cased learner name computed in JS at issue time) and match the lower-cased query against it, or register a Unicode-aware lower() function and use it on both sides.

findings.title: Generator CLI prints a raw Node stack trace for several bad invocations
findings.description:
parseArgs errors and database-open errors are not caught, so some mistakes produce an uncaught-exception stack trace instead of the one-line message the script gives for other bad input (for example '--count must be a positive integer'). The exit code is 1 and nothing is written in every case.

Affected: `--count -5` (ERR_PARSE_ARGS_INVALID_OPTION_VALUE), an unknown flag such as `--bogus` (ERR_PARSE_ARGS_UNKNOWN_OPTION), a stray positional argument (ERR_PARSE_ARGS_UNEXPECTED_POSITIONAL), `--db <directory>` (SQLITE_CANTOPEN), `--db <non-SQLite file>` (SQLITE_NOTADB), and DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS=abc.
findings.expected: A one-line usage or error message, as the script already prints for --count abc and --seed x.
findings.location: backend/scripts/generate-certificates.js:19-30 (parseArgs outside any try) and :49-50 (openInitializedDatabase outside the try block)
findings.reproduction:
node backend/scripts/generate-certificates.js --db /path/g1.sqlite --count -5 -> stack trace ending "code: 'ERR_PARSE_ARGS_INVALID_OPTION_VALUE'", exit=1.

node backend/scripts/generate-certificates.js --db /path/g1.sqlite --bogus -> 'ERR_PARSE_ARGS_UNKNOWN_OPTION', exit=1.

node backend/scripts/generate-certificates.js --db /some/directory --count 5 -> stack trace "code: 'SQLITE_CANTOPEN'", exit=1.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap parseArgs and the database open in try/catch and print the usage line or a one-line error before exiting with status 1.

result.summary: All ten first-round items (T1-T4, C1-C6) are really fixed in the current code, and A1, A2, A3 and A7 held exactly under everything I threw at the new write path: about 43,000 requests over one to three server processes (both SQLite drivers, mixed) with a chaos lock holder, client aborts, 23 kill -9 restarts and SIGTERM produced no double execution, no overwritten result, no differing 201 body and no rows from 4xx/503 answers. The diff is complete (the trees differ only in the listed files) and the 105 tests pass on both drivers. I found no critical or major defect; what remains is two minor items (a queued request gets 503 for an operation that has already completed; the start-up race test rarely detects the defect it guards) and three nits.
checksPerformed: Scope and baseline: read README.md, the whole 2,091-line diff and every changed source file. Compared baseline and deliverable trees: same file list, package-lock.json identical, 17 files outside the diff byte-identical. The deliverable directory was not touched (data/ still holds only .gitkeep). All work ran in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/61a877e9-483e-575a-b7cf-c5b8e94decb9/scratchpad/audit2/concurrency-regression (scripts in its scripts/ folder).
Test suite in my copy: 105/105 pass with better-sqlite3 (28.5 s) and with SQLITE_DRIVER=node (34.2 s).

T1 fixed: 13 variants of sort/order/status using prototype names (constructor, __proto__, toString, valueOf, hasOwnProperty, isPrototypeOf, __defineGetter__, mixed case, '-' prefix) answer 400 invalid_request on both the list and the export; 11 other endpoints fed prototype names answer 200/400/404, never 500.

T2 fixed: bulk-issue bodies nested 1,000 / 10,000 / 20,000 / 45,000 arrays deep and 1,000 / 10,000 objects deep answer 201, the retry replays the identical body, one level deeper answers 409; a 45,000-element wide body answers 201; a revoke body with a 40,000-deep reason answers 400; bodies with own keys __proto__ / constructor / toString are fingerprinted as ordinary payloads.

T3 fixed: 14 revocation reasons (NUL, BEL, ESC, DEL, VT, FF, BS, lone high and low surrogates, non-strings) answer 400 and leave certificate 4 active with no audit event; q/search/status/sort/order/action with %00, %1B, %0A, %09, %7F answer 400 on list and export. Observations, not reported: raw invalid UTF-8 bytes in a JSON body are decoded to U+FFFD by the body parser and stored as valid text; C1 controls such as U+0085 are accepted.

T4 fixed, schema (g): PRAGMA foreign_key_list shows every reference between tenant-owned tables as composite (x_id, tenant_id). With raw SQL on a copy (foreign_keys=ON) 34 cross-tenant attempts were all refused: INSERT and UPDATE through each foreign key of enrollments, bulk_issue_operations, certificates (6 keys) and audit_events (4 keys), moving parents with children, tenant 99, INSERT OR REPLACE over another tenant's id. Same-tenant controls were accepted; foreign_key_check stayed empty.

C1 fixed, both drivers: with another process holding the write lock for 3.5 s and DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS=1000, 20 rounds of list, detail, replay (201, identical body, replayed=true), 409 for a different payload, repeat revoke (200 alreadyRevoked), revoke of a missing id (404) and cross-tenant bulk issue (404) were answered in at most 14.7 ms. A new bulk issue and a new revoke got 503 + Retry-After: 1 after 1,006 / 1,010 ms, row counts were unchanged, and the same key then ran with 201 replayed=false.

C2 fixed, (d): 25 unreadable or different bodies (invalid JSON, primitives, array, {}, empty, none, whitespace, 150 kB, charset latin1/utf-16, unknown content-encoding, corrupt gzip, trailing garbage, other course, alias, extra field, unknown and cross-tenant course) each sent with Alice's used key, an unused key, Bob with Alice's key, a second East admin (inserted by SQL) with Alice's key, and no key. Used key: always 409 idempotency_key_reused. All others: the plain 400/413/415/404 and never a 409 until that actor had used the key itself; nothing was written by any rejected request.

(d) continued: 8 logically identical encodings (whitespace, 1.0, duplicate key, text/plain, form content type, gzip, deflate, brotli) replay the stored body. Key header variants: padded key matches, different case is a different key, malformed key gives 400. 15 raw-socket cases (chunked valid / split / invalid JSON / oversized without Content-Length, Content-Length 0, no length, Expect: 100-continue with good and bad body, both CL and TE, negative CL, CL shorter than the body, body that stops half-way, bad chunk size) behave as expected, except the framing-level cases reported as a nit.

C3 fixed, verified by mutation in a separate copy: removing the under-lock idempotency re-check makes both new cross-process overlap tests fail; making writeTransaction block inside SQLite fails 4 tests; removing the lock-free fast paths fails 3 tests.

C4 fixed: 105 rounds of 5 to 8 real server processes started at once on a new file (better-sqlite3, node, mixed, and with init-db and init-db --reset running at the same moment): every process came up, data pristine, 'Created demo data' logged by exactly one. A tighter harness (processes spin to the same millisecond, then call openInitializedDatabase): 150 rounds / 680 opens on the deliverable with 0 failures and exactly one seeding per round; the same harness on a mutant without the WAL-switch retry fails with 'database is locked' in 19 of 30 rounds (better-sqlite3) and 17 of 20 (node).

C5 fixed, reset literally 'in place': under a running server the inode is unchanged, rows are pristine, the server serves 7 East certificates, ids and serial numbers restart (next issue is again certificate 12 / EAST-0000008), and the old idempotency key runs afresh. With the lock held and DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS=500 the reset exits 1 after 0.55 s with 'Nothing was changed', identical inode and row counts, and the server still replays its stored operation. With a 2 s lock it waits 1.4 s and succeeds.

Reset in other situations: during a deliberately slow 100,000-row export the reset succeeds in 2.1 s, the server serves fresh data at once, and the export completes with all 100,010 lines of its old snapshot (file shrink is deferred until the reader is gone; the WAL stayed at 77 MB for a while). Racing with queued bulk issues and revokes (5 rounds), with the generator (4 rounds, either order), and two resets + generator + generator --clear + init-db at once: all exit 0, invariants hold, no server error.

Reset on odd files: missing file and missing directory are created; a non-database file gives exit 1 'Reset failed, nothing was changed' with an unchanged SHA-256 and no side files; a zero-byte file is initialised; user_version 1 and 3 are deleted and recreated with the documented warning; user_version 2 with a foreign schema is refused and left unchanged.

C6 fixed: a taken port gives one line 'Port 5120 is already in use...' and exit 1 on both drivers, with HOST set, and with another DB path; bad PORT, PORT=70000, unresolvable or non-local HOST, a non-database file and a directory as DB path each give a one-line message and exit 1. Invalid DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS and SQLITE_DRIVER print a stack trace (nit).

(b) randomized stress, validated per key against the SQLite file (one operation row per tenant/admin/key, stored response_body equal to what callers received, at most one replayed=false, only one payload ever gets 201, no row when all answers were 4xx/503, follow-up replay identical, plus the global invariants: certificates unique per tenant/course/learner, exactly one certificate.issued event per certificate, one certificate.revoked event exactly when revoked, foreign_key_check and integrity_check clean). Six runs, 2,400 rounds, 34,911 requests on 1 to 3 servers (DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS 250-300) with a locker holding 0-1.5 s and adding fresh eligible learners, same-key different payloads, unreadable bodies, cross-tenant requests and client aborts: 0 violations, every 503 carried Retry-After, slowest answer 331 ms, no server error logged.
kill -9 under stress: two further runs (550 rounds, 8,206 requests) while a script killed and restarted a random server 23 times: 0 violations, invariants intact.

Deterministic crash scenarios on three driver combinations: kill -9 a server while 11 requests wait (the other server executes once, 7 replays, one effective revocation, restarted server replays); kill -9 a server in the middle of a 30,001-certificate bulk issue while another server waits with the same key (nothing of the killed transaction survives, the waiter executes all 30,001 itself); SIGTERM while 7 requests wait (exit code 0 in 4-8 ms, no error output, keys not burned); the other writer killed with 5,000 uncommitted rows (waiters complete identically, the rows are gone).

(c) 503 semantics and (h) writeTransaction in isolation, both drivers, 18 checks each: timeout gives a busy error after the configured time, PRAGMA busy_timeout is back at the regular value afterwards and between attempts, depth returns to 0, five waiters on one connection each run once after release, a throwing or async callback rolls back, timeoutMs 0 fails at once, a read transaction on the same connection works while a write waits, savepoint failure is contained, constraint errors are not treated as busy, a closed connection gives a non-busy error.

No spin and no stall: with 300 and 2,000 writes waiting for a held lock the server used 10% / 32% of one core and list requests had a 2.1 ms median (max 75 / 450 ms); all waiters completed after release. Reads while the generator and db:reset alternated on a 100,000-row database: 7,742 requests, max 65.6 ms, no non-200. Reads while bulk issues and revokes ran through 18 resets: 4,550 requests, max 42.6 ms, no 5xx other than 503. A write sent during a 250,000-row generator run waited 6.2 s and completed.

(e) revocation under contention: in the stress runs each targeted certificate got at most one alreadyRevoked=false, identical revokedAt for all callers, exactly one revoked audit event, a 404 for the other tenant, and stayed active with no event when every answer was 503.

UI (Playwright, built frontend, lock held): a double click sends one POST; the button stays locked; after the 503 the page says 'The bulk issue for Safety 101 has not run yet' with Retry safely; three POSTs carried one idempotency key; after release the retry shows 2 issued and no replay note.
Documented commands at the default path in my copy: npm start, npm run generate:east and npm run db:reset under the running server all worked (inode unchanged, 100,009 then 7 East certificates).

Observed and not reported as defects: when two different payloads with one key are both queued, the one that gets the lock first wins and the other gets 409 (not arrival order); a client that disconnects while its request waits does not cancel the operation, and its retry replays.

findings.title: A request already queued for the write lock gets 503 although the identical request has completed and its result is readable without the lock
findings.description: The lock-free lookup of the idempotency key (and of the certificate status in revoke) runs once, before the request starts waiting. If an identical request commits while this one waits and another process takes the write lock again for longer than the remaining wait, the waiting caller is told 503 database_busy. At that moment the operation has completed and a new identical request is replayed in 2-4 ms. So two concurrent identical callers get different answers (201 and 503), and the UI would show 'has not run yet' for an operation that did run. Nothing is executed twice and a retry replays, hence minor. It needs a second long lock hold, for example two maintenance commands back to back or a second server running long bulk issues.
findings.expected: README section 6 (A2): 'A key that has already run is answered from a plain read, without queueing for the write lock'; README section 7: 'reads, replays and already-revoked answers are served as usual'; A2: 'All callers receive the same logical outcome.' A queued request should be answered from the stored result before it gives up.
findings.reproduction: Two servers on one database: PORT=5121 and PORT=5122 with DB_PATH=<db> DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS=1500 node backend/src/server.js. (1) scripts/lock.py <db> 0.5 holds BEGIN IMMEDIATE for 0.5 s. (2) scripts/relock.py <db> key:<K> 2.2 polls every 1 ms for the operation row with key K and takes BEGIN IMMEDIATE for 2.2 s as soon as it exists. (3) r1 = POST :5121/api/bulk-issues {"courseId":4} with Idempotency-Key K as bob@west.test; 150 ms later r2 = the same request to :5122. (4) once the second lock is held, r3 = the same request again to :5122. Driver: scripts/late503.mjs 5121 5122 <db> 6. Observed in 6 of 6 rounds, e.g. 'r1 201 replayed=false (531 ms) | r2 (was waiting) 503 database_busy (1504 ms) | r3 201 replayed=true (3 ms)'; in 2 rounds the roles of r1 and r2 were swapped. Same with revoke of certificate 9: 'r1 503 | r2 200 alreadyRevoked=false (331 ms) | r3 200 alreadyRevoked=true (2 ms)'. Database invariants stayed intact (one operation per key).
findings.suggestedFix: Before turning the busy error into a 503 (or on each poll of the wait loop), repeat the lock-free lookup: answerFromStoredKey() in bulkIssue and the status read in revoke, and answer from it when it now finds the stored result or the revoked certificate.

findings.title: The start-up race test rarely detects the defect it guards (C4); the unit test passes even when openDatabase no longer retries
findings.description: The fix for simultaneous start-up is effective, but its regression tests would mostly not notice if it were lost. The unit test exercises enableWal() only with a stand-in connection, so it does not check that openDatabase() uses it. The acceptance test starts 3 servers 4 times through startServer, which seldom hits the collision window on this machine. With the retry removed from openDatabase, all 33 unit tests pass and the acceptance test passed in 11 of 12 runs.
findings.expected: README section 6 lists these tests as the verification of start-up on a new file; a test that claims to guard the 'one of them crashed' defect should fail reliably when the retry is removed.
findings.reproduction: In a separate copy, replace the try { enableWal(connection) } catch block in backend/src/db/sqlite.js (openDatabase) with connection.exec('PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL'), as before the fix. Then: node --test test/unit.test.js gives 33 pass, 0 fail. Run 12 times: node --test --test-concurrency=1 --test-name-pattern="servers started at the same moment" test/acceptance.test.js gives 11 passes, 1 failure ('Could not open the database ...: database is locked'). For comparison, scripts/openrace.mjs (4 processes import bootstrap.js, spin until the same millisecond, then call openInitializedDatabase on a new file) fails on that mutant in 19 of 30 rounds (better-sqlite3) and 17 of 20 (node), and in 0 of 150 rounds on the deliverable.
findings.suggestedFix: Synchronise the openers in the test: child processes that load the modules first, wait for a shared start instant, then open the new file, repeated a few dozen times. Alternatively add a test that openDatabase() survives a busy answer to the journal-mode switch.

findings.title: Invalid DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS (and SQLITE_DRIVER) crash start-up with a stack trace instead of the one-line message
findings.description: The new setting DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS is validated at module load of sqlite.js, before server.js reaches its try/catch, so a bad value prints a Node stack trace. SQLITE_DRIVER behaves the same way (that part predates this change). The message itself is readable, so this is cosmetic, but the change set claims one-line start-up errors and the README documents the setting. The CLI scripts print the same trace.
findings.expected: server.js: 'Start-up problems are the operator's to fix: say what is wrong in one line, without a stack trace'; the test 'invalid settings and unusable database files are reported the same way' covers only PORT.
findings.reproduction: PORT=5121 DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS=abc DB_PATH=<db> node backend/src/server.js prints 'file:///.../backend/src/db/sqlite.js:27  throw new Error(`DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS must be an integer between 0 and 600000 milliseconds ...' followed by 'at lockWaitFromEnv ... at ModuleJob.run ...' and 'Node.js v22.23.5', exit 1. Same for DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS=-1 and SQLITE_DRIVER=postgres. For contrast, PORT=eighty prints the single line 'PORT must be an integer between 0 and 65535 (got "eighty")'.
findings.suggestedFix: Read and validate both settings lazily (in loadConfig or openDatabase), or load the database module with a dynamic import inside the try block of server.js.

findings.title: A body that stops half-way or has broken chunk framing gets Node's bare 400, not 409, even when its key has been used
findings.description: When the request body is truncated at the transport level (fewer bytes than Content-Length and then FIN, a chunked body without its terminating chunk, a malformed chunk size), Node's HTTP layer answers 'HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request' with no JSON body and closes the socket before bulkIssueBody can send its 409. Nothing is written and the stored result is intact. Every unreadable body that arrives as a complete HTTP request does get 409, so this is only an inaccuracy of the unconditional README wording.
findings.expected: README section 6 (A3): 'A body that cannot be read at all (malformed, oversized, unsupported encoding) is a different request too and gets the same 409 once its key has been used.'
findings.reproduction:
After a 201 for key used-1, send over a raw socket: 'POST /api/bulk-issues HTTP/1.1', Host, X-Actor-Email: alice@east.test, Content-Type: application/json, Idempotency-Key: used-1, Content-Length: 14, blank line, then only the 8 bytes '{"course' followed by a write-side shutdown. Response: b'HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Connection: close

'. The same response comes for Transfer-Encoding: chunked with chunk size 'zz', and for a chunked body that ends after '5
{"cou

findings.suggestedFix: Qualify the README sentence (a complete request whose body cannot be parsed), or leave as is; handling 'clientError' for this is not worth the complexity.

findings.title: The lock-wait deadline follows the wall clock, so a clock step changes how long a request waits
findings.description: writeTransaction computes its deadline with Date.now(). If the system clock is set back while a request waits (manual correction, NTP step), the request keeps waiting for the configured time plus the size of the step; a forward step makes it give up early. I did not change the machine's clock: the step was simulated by patching Date.now in an isolated script that imports the deliverable's sqlite.js.
findings.expected: README section 5: 503 'when another process has held the database's write lock for longer than DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS'; the wait should be bounded by elapsed time.
findings.reproduction: scripts/clock.mjs: open two connections with openDatabase(), hold BEGIN IMMEDIATE on one, call db.writeTransaction(fn, { timeoutMs: 300 }) on the other and shift a patched Date.now 100 ms into the wait. Output: 'no step: ... busy error after 300 ms'; 'clock set back 3 s: ... busy error after 3301 ms'; 'clock set forward 3 s: ... busy error after 126 ms'.
findings.suggestedFix: Use performance.now() (monotonic) for the deadline in writeTransaction and enableWal.

result.summary: I drove all four UI workflows of spec section 3 in Chromium via Playwright against a private copy (production build on a seeded DB and on a 100,000-row East DB, plus the Vite dev build for React warnings), and read frontend/src for logic errors. The core behaviour holds: no acceptance criterion failed through the UI, CSV exports matched the active search/status/sort exactly (checked independently against SQLite with Python zoneinfo), tenant data never rendered under the wrong actor, and retries reused the same Idempotency-Key. I found seven limited defects, none above minor: duplicate-submission protection and operation status are lost on a tab round trip, two places where the UI asserts a write did not happen when it did, a stale-response race in "View outcomes", ASCII-only case-insensitive search, a blank page on a malformed 200 response, and two nits. The 105-test suite contains no frontend tests, so none of the UI behaviour is covered by `npm test`.
checksPerformed: Build and start: `npm run build` in the private copy succeeded; `PORT=5404 npm start` (the documented single command) installed, built, seeded and served UI + API; `npm run generate:east -- --db <file>` produced 100,007 East certificates in 3.2 s.

Browser console: no React warnings or page errors in any workflow on the production build or on the Vite dev build (React development mode + StrictMode); the only console entries were the expected 'Failed to load resource' lines for deliberately failed requests.

List basics (PASS): actor switch changes tenant chip, document title and rows (EAST-/WEST- serials only); search by learner name ('alex') and by serial ('EAST-0000003'); status filter; all five column-header sorts toggle asc/desc and stay in sync with the Sort-by select; selected actor survives reload; an unknown e-mail in localStorage falls back to the first actor.

List states (PASS): loading spinner on first load, dimmed table with 'Loading…' overlay on refresh, filtered empty state with 'Clear search and filters', unfiltered empty state with 'Go to bulk issue', error state for HTTP 500 / network failure / non-JSON 200 / truncated JSON with a working 'Try again'; pagination is hidden in the error state. Boot failure of /api/actors shows 'The console could not start' with a working retry.

List races (PASS): a slow response for q='m' arriving after the fast response for q='mei' never overwrote the newer rows; typing 9 characters at 60 ms intervals issued exactly one request; Enter applies the search immediately without a duplicate request from the debounce; trailing spaces cause no extra request.

Actor switch with requests in flight (PASS): with Alice's list request delayed 1.5 s and an immediate switch to Bob, only WEST rows were ever rendered over 2.5 s of polling; six rapid switches with random delays ended consistent. Observation: switching actor with a drawer open fires one transient `GET /api/certificates/<previous tenant's id>` under the new actor (server answers 404; a MutationObserver saw only 'Loading certificate…' before the drawer closed) - no data leak.

Pagination (PASS, 100k DB): 'Page 1 of 4,001', Last page shows 100,001-100,007; a filter change on page 4,001 or page 3 issues a single request for page=1 of the new filter; page-size change resets to page 1; after revoking the only row of the last page under status=active the list stepped back from page 2 of 2 to page 1 of 1; input is capped at 100 characters, matching the server limit.

CSV export correctness (PASS): UI downloads for (q=kelly, sort learner asc), (typed 'stewart' and clicked Export immediately, inside the debounce window), (q=EAST-00123 + status revoked + Issued header toggled to asc) and (header sort changed and Export clicked with no wait) each matched the list API row for row; the table also switched to the exported filter. Header is Learner Name, Course Title, Serial Number, Issue Date (Australia/Sydney).

CSV export independent check (PASS): the full 100,007-row UI export matched SQLite rows ordered by (Sydney-local date, instant, id) descending, with local times recomputed by Python zoneinfo - 0 mismatches; the kelly/learner export matched an independent Python sort (1,930 rows, 0 mismatches); EAST-0000001 exports as 2026-01-11 00:30 and Bob's WEST-0000001 as 2026-01-10 21:30.

Export scale and concurrency (PASS): full 100k export through the UI took about 0.3 s (7.3 MB), two consecutive exports were byte-identical, and six list page navigations during the export took 24-48 ms each.

Export failures (PASS): double click sends one request and one download; HTTP 500 and connection reset show 'Export failed: …' with a working 'Try again'; a response truncated after 1 MB (through my own cutting proxy) was reported as failed and no file was saved.

Detail drawer (PASS): shows serial, learner, course, tenant-local issue date with UTC offset and UTC instant, status and audit trail; East cert 1 shows 2026-01-11 00:30, West cert 8 shows 2026-01-10 21:30; Escape closes it, browser Back reopens, Forward closes, reload keeps the deep link.
Cross-tenant deep links (PASS): #/certificates/8 as Alice and #/certificates/1 as Bob show 'Certificate not found'; a 21-digit id shows not found; #/certificates/abc opens no drawer.

Revocation confirmation (PASS): Cancel, Escape and backdrop click each close only the confirmation, leave the drawer open and send no request; Enter inside the reason textarea does not submit; a 500 keeps the dialog and the typed reason and offers 'Try again'; a double click on confirm during a 1 s delayed request sent exactly one POST; Escape/backdrop are ignored and both buttons disabled while in flight.

Revocation result (PASS): status flips to Revoked, revoked-by/time/reason and the new audit entry appear, the Revoke button disappears, the list reloads once and the row shows Revoked; exactly one certificate.revoked audit event; state persists across reload. Revoking a certificate already revoked elsewhere shows 'had already been revoked; nothing was changed' with still one audit event. Browser Back during an in-flight revoke closes the drawer and the list still refreshes when it completes.

Revocation with the SQLite write lock held (PASS): with BEGIN IMMEDIATE held by a Python script and DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS=1500 the dialog showed 'The certificate was not revoked: The database is busy…' with no audit event; 'Try again' after release revoked with one audit event.

Bulk issue basics (PASS): course list is tenant-specific for Alice and Bob; roster preview and 'Issue 2 certificates' label; double click, Enter+Enter and clicks during the request send one POST; button shows 'Issuing…', course select is disabled in flight, status banner is shown; result lists 2 issued / 3 skipped with reasons and serial links; outcome filter chips work; roster and history refresh; button becomes 'No eligible learners'.

Bulk issue lost response (PASS): server executed but the response was dropped - UI says 'may or may not have gone through'; 'Retry safely' re-sent the same key, the replay note was shown, and counts stayed at +1 certificate / +1 audit / 1 operation. A 502 with an HTML body is also treated as retryable. A new operation gets a new key.

Bulk issue edge paths: switching actor mid-flight completes Bob's request server-side and renders nothing under Alice; changing course while a retry decision is pending discards the retry prompt (result is then only reachable through Recent operations); a 10,000-learner bulk issue through the UI took 0.8 s with one POST, previewed 200 rows and 'Show all' rendered 10,000; roster pagination on a 10,000-learner course works and resets on course change.
Insecure origin (PASS): loaded via http://192.0.2.2:5400 where crypto.randomUUID is undefined - the getRandomValues fallback produced a valid UUID key and both bulk issue and export worked.

Code read of frontend/src (App.jsx, api.js, hooks.js, CertificatesPage.jsx, CertificateDetail.jsx, BulkIssuePage.jsx, ui.jsx): useQuery aborts on dependency change and unmount; page state is keyed by the filter; main content is keyed by actor so page state resets between tenants; all async handlers catch their rejections. Defects found by reading are listed as findings.
Test coverage: backend/test has no frontend or browser tests (the helper points STATIC_DIR at a non-existent folder), so none of the UI behaviour above is verified by `npm test`.
