findings.title: Leaving and re-entering the Bulk issue tab during a request drops the submission lock and operation status; a second click sends a second bulk issue with a new Idempotency-Key
findings.criterion: Spec 3.2 (Bulk Issue: prevent duplicate UI submissions and show operation status)
findings.description: The in-flight guard (`inFlight` ref), the `run` state and the attempt's idempotency key live only in BulkIssuePage component state. App.jsx renders either BulkIssuePage or CertificatesPage by hash route, so clicking the Certificates tab (or a serial link in the roster) and coming back unmounts the page while the POST is still pending. On return the status banner is gone, no course is selected, and after re-selecting the course the button reads 'Issue 2 certificates' and is enabled. Clicking it sends a second POST with a freshly generated key. The server keeps the data safe (one of the two operations issues, the other skips everyone), but two operations are recorded for one intention, the user may be shown either result, and the README statement 'The button locks while the request is in flight, the operation status is shown' does not hold across this navigation. The window is realistic: a bulk issue waits up to DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS (default 10 s) while the generator or db:reset holds the write lock.
findings.expected: Spec 3.2: 'Prevent duplicate UI submissions and show operation status.' The pending operation (and its key) should survive in-app navigation, or the page should at least not offer a new submission while one is pending.
findings.reproduction: Server on the seeded DB with default DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS, no request interception (script t/t16.cjs). 1) Hold the write lock: `python3 hold.py small.sqlite 5` (BEGIN IMMEDIATE, sleep 5, ROLLBACK). 2) UI as Alice: Bulk issue, choose Safety 101, click 'Issue 2 certificates' -> state 'submitting', button disabled. 3) Click tab 'Certificates', then tab 'Bulk issue', choose Safety 101 again. Observed: operation-status data-state='idle', button 'Issue 2 certificates' enabled. 4) Click it. Observed POST keys: ['82e3d0fb-bb73-4595-803c-92c6b46f16c3', 'af643b70-5b16-4d40-a558-0098599eb013'] (two different keys); server operations afterwards: '#2 issued=0 skipped=5', '#1 issued=2 skipped=3'; certs 9, audit 10 (no duplicate certificates). Same result with a 2.5 s page.route delay instead of the lock (t/t11.cjs).
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the pending attempt (course, key, status) above the routed pages (in App or a small store, optionally sessionStorage) so the page re-attaches to it on remount, or keep BulkIssuePage mounted while hidden.

findings.title: Bulk issue whose 201 response body is cut off or unreadable is reported as 'was rejected' with no safe retry, although the certificates were issued
findings.criterion: Spec 3.2 (operation status) / README section 3 ('If the answer is lost (network error, 5xx), Retry safely repeats the request')
findings.location: frontend/src/api.js:97-108 (bulkIssue: `await response.json()` outside the ApiError mapping); frontend/src/components/BulkIssuePage.jsx:168,281-301
findings.description: `send()` only converts a failed `fetch()` into `ApiError(0, 'network_error')`. If the connection drops after the headers, or the body is not valid JSON, `response.json()` rejects with a plain TypeError/SyntaxError. That error has no `retryable` property, so BulkIssuePage falls into the last branch: the heading says 'The bulk issue for <course> was rejected', the raw message ('Failed to fetch' / 'Unterminated string in JSON…') is shown, and no 'Retry safely' button is offered - the idempotency key of the attempt is discarded on Dismiss. In fact the server committed the operation. The UI therefore states that a write did not happen when it did, and the documented lost-answer path is not taken for this kind of lost answer.
findings.expected: An answer that could not be read is an unknown outcome: show 'may or may not have gone through' and offer 'Retry safely' with the same Idempotency-Key (README section 3).
findings.reproduction: (a) Through a small proxy of mine that forwards to the server but destroys the socket 50 bytes into the POST /api/bulk-issues response (t/proxy.cjs + t/t8.cjs): choose Safety 101, click Issue. Observed banner: '[failed] The bulk issue for Safety 101 was rejected | Failed to fetch | Dismiss', retry button absent; server before: 100007 certificates / 0 operations, after: 100009 / 1. (b) With page.route doing `route.fetch()` and fulfilling with the real status/headers and the first 60 bytes of the body (t/t7.cjs): banner 'The bulk issue for Safety 101 was rejected | Unterminated string in JSON at position 60', retry button absent, server certs=9 audit=10 ops=1 (2 issued).
findings.suggestedFix: In api.js wrap body reading (`response.json()`, `response.blob()`) so that any failure after a 2xx status becomes `ApiError(0, 'network_error', …)`; in BulkIssuePage treat every non-ApiError as retryable/unknown.

findings.title: Search is case-insensitive only for ASCII letters: 'álvarez' or 'JOSÉ' does not find the seeded learner 'José Álvarez'
findings.criterion: Spec 3.1 (Certificate List: search by learner name)
findings.description: The search uses SQLite LIKE, which folds case for ASCII only. The UI search therefore behaves case-insensitively for names like O'Connor ('O'CONNOR' matches) but case-sensitively for accented letters. The demo data itself contains 'José Álvarez': typing the surname in lower case, or the first name in upper case, shows the 'No certificates match your search' empty state. The same filter feeds the CSV export, so the export is empty too. The spec does not define case handling, so this is an inconsistency of the implemented behaviour rather than a spec violation.
findings.expected: Consistent matching: either fully case-insensitive (including non-ASCII letters) or documented as ASCII-only.
findings.reproduction: UI as Alice on the seeded DB (t/t9.cjs): type 'álvarez' -> 'No certificates'; 'Álvarez' -> '1–1 of 1 certificates'; 'JOSÉ' -> 'No certificates'; 'josé' -> '1–1 of 1 certificates'. API: `curl -s -G -H 'X-Actor-Email: alice@east.test' --data-urlencode 'q=álvarez' localhost:5400/api/certificates` -> total 0; q=Álvarez -> total 1; q=O'CONNOR -> total 2 (ASCII folding works).
findings.suggestedFix: Store a normalised search column (e.g. `learner_name` lower-cased with JS `toLocaleLowerCase()` at write time) and compare against the lower-cased query, or register a Unicode-aware lower() function.

findings.title: 'View outcomes' has no stale-response protection: a slower earlier click replaces the operation the user opened last
findings.description: viewOperation awaits `api.getOperation(id)` and unconditionally calls setViewed with whatever resolves, without an AbortController or a check that `id` is still the requested one. Every other loader in the app goes through useQuery, which cancels outdated requests; this one does not. If the user clicks 'View outcomes' on one operation and then on another, and the first answer arrives later, the panel switches back to the first operation. The heading shows the number of the operation actually displayed, so the data is not mislabelled, but it is not the operation the user last asked for. Related cosmetic issue: opening 'View outcomes' for the operation that was just run renders two result panels with the same DOM id 'result-heading' and the same data-testid.
findings.expected: The panel shows the operation selected last; outdated responses are discarded, as the list and roster already do.
findings.reproduction: t/t7.cjs, Alice with operations #1 and #2 in Recent operations; page.route delays GET /api/bulk-issues/1 by 1.2 s. Click 'View outcomes' on #1, 100 ms later on #2. Observed after 0.5 s: heading 'Operation #2 · First Aid Refresher'; 1.5 s later: 'Operation #1 · Safety 101'. Duplicate ids observed in t/t12.cjs: after a run, clicking View outcomes gives 2 elements with id=result-heading.
findings.suggestedFix: Track the latest requested id (ref or AbortController) and ignore responses for any other id; hide the 'viewed' panel when it is the same operation as the current run result.

findings.title: No error boundary: a 200 response with unexpected JSON blanks the entire console
findings.criterion: Spec 3.1 (show loading, empty and error states)
findings.description: The list render and the step-back effect dereference `data.items` without checking the shape, and nothing in the tree catches render exceptions. When /api/certificates answers 200 with valid JSON of another shape (`{"foo":1}` or `null`), React unmounts the whole root: the page is completely blank, there is no error state and no retry, only a reload helps. Non-JSON and truncated bodies are handled correctly (error state with 'Try again'). I could not make the real server produce such a response, so the trigger is a faulty intermediary or a future API change; the defect is the missing safety net.
findings.expected: A malformed answer should land in the documented error state ('errors offer Try again', README section 3), not in a blank page.
findings.reproduction: t/t2b.cjs: load the list, then `page.route('**/api/certificates?**', r => r.fulfill({status:200, contentType:'application/json', body:'{"foo":1}'}))` and change the status filter. Observed: `#root` has 0 children; pageerror "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')". With body 'null': pageerror "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'items')", root empty. With an HTML body or truncated JSON the error state is shown correctly.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate the response shape in api.js (throw an ApiError when `items` is not an array) and add a top-level error boundary that renders ErrorState with a reload action.

findings.title: Revoke dialog says 'The certificate was not revoked' when the outcome is unknown; after a lost response the certificate is in fact revoked
findings.description: Every failure of the revoke request is rendered as 'The certificate was not revoked: <message>'. For a network error or a 5xx the outcome is unknown. When the server executed the revocation and only the response was lost, the dialog asserts the opposite of the real state; 'Try again' then reports 'This certificate had already been revoked; nothing was changed.' The end state and the audit trail are correct (one event), only the wording is wrong. The bulk-issue page distinguishes 'has not run yet' / 'may or may not have gone through' / 'was rejected'; the revoke dialog does not.
findings.expected: For status 0 / 5xx say that the outcome is unknown and that repeating is safe; reserve 'was not revoked' for 4xx and 503 database_busy.
findings.reproduction: t/t11.cjs: open #/certificates/4 as Alice; page.route on POST /api/certificates/4/revoke performs `route.fetch()` (server executes) and then `route.abort('connectionreset')`. Click Revoke certificate…, confirm. Observed alert: 'The certificate was not revoked: The server could not be reached. Check that it is running, then try again.' while GET /api/certificates/4 already returns status 'revoked'. Click 'Try again': 'This certificate had already been revoked; nothing was changed.'; audit events for 4: certificate.revoked x1, certificate.issued x1.
findings.suggestedFix: Use `error.retryable` (as BulkIssuePage does) to choose between 'was not revoked' and 'may or may not have been revoked - trying again is safe'.

findings.title: A pasted tab character in the search box turns the list (and the export) into a hard error whose 'Try again' can never succeed
findings.criterion: Spec 3.1 (search by learner name or serial number)
findings.description: The server rejects control characters in `q` with 400 (documented). The UI trims the text but forwards interior control characters unchanged, so pasting two adjacent spreadsheet cells ('Alex Lee<TAB>Safety 101') replaces the table with the load-failure panel 'Certificates could not be loaded … Query parameter "q" contains characters that are not allowed … HTTP 400 · invalid_request' and a 'Try again' button that repeats the same failing request. Export fails the same way. An input problem is presented as a server failure with a futile retry.
findings.expected: Either normalise control characters to spaces before sending, or show an input hint next to the search box instead of the load-error state.
findings.reproduction: t/t17.cjs: `navigator.clipboard.writeText('Alex Lee\tSafety 101')`, focus the search input, Ctrl+V. Observed input value "Alex Lee\tSafety 101"; list area: '! | Certificates could not be loaded | Query parameter "q" contains characters that are not allowed (control characters or malformed Unicode) | HTTP 400 · invalid_request | Try again'; after clicking Try again data-state is still 'error'; Export CSV: no download, 'Export failed: Query parameter "q" contains characters that are not allowed…'.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace /[\u0000-\u001f\u007f]+/g with a space in the search text before trimming.

findings.title: An export still in flight when the actor is switched downloads the previous tenant's file under the new tenant, with no status shown
findings.location: frontend/src/api.js:111-127 (exportCsv has no AbortSignal and triggers the download itself); frontend/src/components/CertificatesPage.jsx:63-74
findings.description: exportCsv is not cancellable and performs `link.click()` inside the API helper. When the actor is switched while an export is pending, CertificatesPage is remounted for the new tenant (export button enabled, no status line), and about a second later the browser saves 'certificates-east-….csv' while the header shows tenant West. The file contains only what Alice requested, so this is not an isolation breach, but a file of tenant A appears while the console is acting as tenant B with nothing on screen explaining it.
findings.expected: Abort a pending export when the page for that actor unmounts (as list and detail requests already are), or keep its status visible.
findings.reproduction: t/t4.cjs on the 100k DB with the export request delayed 1.5 s by page.route: as Alice click Export CSV, 200 ms later select bob@west.test. Observed as Bob: export button enabled, export status text ''. 3.5 s later: download event with suggested filename 'certificates-east-20261124-0010.csv' while data-testid=tenant-name shows 'West' and the export status is still empty.
findings.suggestedFix: Pass an AbortSignal to exportCsv and abort it in an unmount effect of CertificatesPage; trigger the download only if the component is still mounted.

findings.title: Search is case-insensitive only for ASCII letters: the seeded learner "José Álvarez" is not found by "álvarez" or "JOSÉ"
findings.criterion: Section 3.1 Certificate List (search by learner name)
findings.location: backend/src/services/certificates.js:111 (LIKE filter shared by list and export); backend/test/acceptance.test.js:1116 (test title claims case-insensitive search)
findings.description: The search filter is `c.learner_name LIKE @pattern`. SQLite's LIKE folds case for the 26 ASCII letters only, so a query matches or misses depending on whether the letter that differs in case is accented. The demo data deliberately contains "José Álvarez": typing the surname in lower case, or the first name in upper case, returns an empty list, while "alex" and "ALEX" both find "Alex Lee". The CSV export uses the same buildFilter, so it has the same blind spot. The author's own test describes the search as case-insensitive but only tries ASCII input. NOCASE sorting has the same ASCII-only folding (a name starting with an accented capital would sort after Z); I did not reproduce that because no seeded name starts with one.
findings.expected: A search described and tested as case-insensitive should find "José Álvarez" for "álvarez" and "JOSÉ", just as it finds "Alex Lee" for "ALEX".
findings.reproduction:
Fresh demo database, server from my copy: cd backend && PORT=5500 DB_PATH=<scratch>/a.sqlite node src/server.js
A='X-Actor-Email: alice@east.test'
curl -s -H "$A" 'localhost:5500/api/certificates?q=%C3%81lvarez'  -> total 1 (José Álvarez)
curl -s -H "$A" 'localhost:5500/api/certificates?q=%C3%A1lvarez'  -> total 0, q echoed as "álvarez"
curl -s -H "$A" 'localhost:5500/api/certificates?q=jos%C3%A9'     -> total 1
curl -s -H "$A" 'localhost:5500/api/certificates?q=JOS%C3%89'     -> total 0, q echoed as "JOSÉ"
curl -s -H "$A" 'localhost:5500/api/certificates?q=%C3%81LVAREZ'  -> total 1 (ASCII part folds, Á matches exactly)
curl -s -H "$A" 'localhost:5500/api/certificates?q=ALEX'          -> total 2
Identical on the node:sqlite server.
findings.suggestedFix: Compare on a normalised key: store a lower-cased copy of learner_name (JS toLowerCase / NFC) in an indexed column and lower-case q the same way, or register a Unicode-aware lower() function on the connection. Add a non-ASCII case to the search test.

findings.title: Stalled or slow export downloads are never capped or timed out; each holds a connection, up to 16 MB of memory and a WAL snapshot
findings.criterion: Section 3.4 CSV Export (general robustness; no acceptance criterion fails)
findings.location: backend/src/app.js:124-159 (one new SQLite connection per export request, no limit); backend/src/server.js:40-58 (no socket or response timeout); backend/src/db/sqlite.js:309-338 (reader keeps the driver's default page cache)
findings.description:
Every export opens its own SQLite connection and read transaction and keeps both for as long as the client keeps the socket open. There is no limit on simultaneous exports and no inactivity timeout, so a client that stops reading holds these resources indefinitely. Three measured consequences:
- Memory: each stalled export costs about 15.9 MB RSS on better-sqlite3 (its 16 MB default page cache fills) and about 5.5 MB on node:sqlite. Forty stalled downloads took a fresh server from 63 MB to 698 MB, and RSS stayed at that high-water mark after they disconnected.
- WAL growth: the open snapshot stops checkpoints, which defeats the journal_size_limit the code sets for this purpose. With one stalled download the WAL grew by about 82 MB per generator run.
- Latency afterwards: the first write after the stall ran the deferred checkpoint inside COMMIT on the server's only thread and delayed concurrent reads.
This does not break A6 (reads are not blocked while the export is stalled), and resources are released when the client disconnects. It needs slow or stalled clients, which the UI's fetch-to-blob download does not produce, so the practical risk for an internal console is low. The README's "Memory use is flat" is true per export only.
findings.expected: Bounded resource use for exports: a cap on concurrent exports and/or an idle timeout on the response, so one non-reading client cannot pin a snapshot and connection without limit.
findings.reproduction:
Scripts in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/61a877e9-483e-575a-b7cf-c5b8e94decb9/scratchpad/audit2/backend-review-fuzz/work (stall.mjs, longstall.mjs, walpin.mjs, ckpt.mjs), database with 100,007 East certificates (generate-certificates.js --count 100000).
1. stall.mjs: open 40 raw sockets, send GET /api/certificates/export.csv?sort=learner with X-Actor-Email: alice@east.test, never read. Fresh better-sqlite3 server: "RSS baseline 63 MB, with 40 stalled exports 698 MB (+15.9 MB each), after disconnect 701 MB". Fresh node:sqlite server: "baseline 60 MB, with 40 stalled exports 278 MB (+5.5 MB each)".
2. longstall.mjs: one stalled export held 90 s. "t=90s: socket closed by server: false; wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE) (busy, log, checkpointed) = (0, 37, 0)"; after resuming it completed with 100,007 rows; only then did the checkpoint complete (0, 44, 44).
3. walpin.mjs: WAL after a generator run with no download in flight: 17 MB. With one stalled download: 82 MB, 163 MB, 245 MB after generator runs 1, 2, 3.
4. ckpt.mjs: after dropping that download, the first write (POST /api/bulk-issues) took 471 ms and five concurrent GET /api/certificates?pageSize=1 took 444-455 ms each (normally 2-7 ms).
findings.suggestedFix: Add res.setTimeout (or a per-export idle timer) that destroys the response and runs the existing cleanup; limit concurrent exports with a small semaphore (429/503 beyond it); set a small PRAGMA cache_size on the reader connection.

findings.title: List/export parameter parsing accepts or mis-reports several inputs, contrary to the "unknown values are rejected" comment
findings.location: backend/src/services/certificates.js:69-87 (sort/order parsing and its comment); backend/src/app.js:56 ('simple' query parser, 1000-key cap of node:querystring); backend/src/lib/params.js:36 with backend/src/services/certificates.js:285-294 (\d{1,9} against max 1e15)
findings.description:
Five small inconsistencies, none reachable from the UI:
(a) `sort=-learner&order=` sorts ascending: the empty order is not nullish, so the leading minus is ignored and the default order applies, while `sort=-learner` alone sorts descending.
(b) `sort=&sortBy=course` sorts by issued: the present-but-empty `sort` shadows the alias.
(c) `sort=issued!!!` and `sort=l-e-a-r-n-e-r` are accepted because every non-letter is stripped before the alias lookup, although the comment on parseListQuery says unknown values are rejected rather than silently ignored.
(d) Query parameters after the 1000th are silently dropped by node:querystring. A URL with 1000 junk parameters followed by `q=...` or `status=...` is answered 200 with the filter ignored: the list and the CSV export return unfiltered data, and an invalid `status` is not rejected.
(e) `GET /api/audit-events?certificateId=1234567890` is rejected as "must be a whole number" although the same parameter's range message advertises ids up to 1000000000000000 and path ids accept 15 digits.
findings.expected: Consistent handling: the minus prefix honoured whenever order is empty, aliases consulted when the primary name is empty, sort values matched exactly (or the comment corrected), an explicit 400 for more than the supported number of parameters, and a digit limit that matches the documented range.
findings.reproduction:
Server on a small demo database (10 East certificates at the time), A='X-Actor-Email: alice@east.test':
curl -s -H "$A" 'localhost:5500/api/certificates?pageSize=3&sort=-learner'        -> order "desc", first Tom Walker
curl -s -H "$A" 'localhost:5500/api/certificates?pageSize=3&sort=-learner&order=' -> order "asc", first Alex Lee
curl -s -H "$A" 'localhost:5500/api/certificates?pageSize=3&sort=&sortBy=course'  -> sort "issued" (sortBy=course alone gives sort "course")
curl -s -H "$A" 'localhost:5500/api/certificates?pageSize=3&sort=issued!!!'      -> 200, sort "issued"
curl -s -H "$A" 'localhost:5500/api/certificates?pageSize=3&sort=l-e-a-r-n-e-r'  -> 200, sort "learner"
MANY=$(python3 -c "print('&'.join(f'p{i}=1' for i in range(1000)))")
curl -s -H "$A" "localhost:5500/api/certificates?q=zzzzqq&status=revoked"        -> total 0
curl -s -H "$A" "localhost:5500/api/certificates?$MANY&q=zzzzqq&status=revoked"  -> total 10, q "", status "all"
curl -s -H "$A" "localhost:5500/api/certificates/export.csv?$MANY&q=zzzzqq"      -> 10 data rows (0 without the junk parameters)
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -H "$A" "localhost:5500/api/certificates?$MANY&status=bogus" -> 200 (400 without the junk parameters)
curl -s -H "$A" 'localhost:5500/api/audit-events?certificateId=1234567890' -> 400 'Query parameter "certificateId" must be a whole number'
curl -s -H "$A" 'localhost:5500/api/audit-events?certificateId=0'          -> 400 '... must be between 1 and 1000000000000000'
findings.suggestedFix: Use `order ||= 'desc'` for the minus prefix; skip empty values when resolving aliases; match the sort key against the alias table without stripping characters; parse the query with an explicit maxKeys and reject requests that exceed it; derive the digit limit in queryInteger from `max`.

findings.title: Invalid DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS / SQLITE_DRIVER and several CLI errors end in raw stack traces instead of the one-line message used for other start-up problems
findings.location: backend/src/db/sqlite.js:23-32 and 81-110 (throw during module evaluation, before server.js:12-29 can report them); backend/scripts/generate-certificates.js:19-29 and :50; backend/scripts/init-db.js:21-23 and :91
findings.description: server.js states that start-up problems are reported in one line without a stack trace, and it does so for PORT, a taken port, an unusable database file and a bad HOST. The two settings read inside db/sqlite.js are validated at import time by top-level code, so a bad value for a README-documented setting (DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS, SQLITE_DRIVER), or a forced driver that cannot be loaded, crashes with a Node stack trace before server.js runs. The two CLI scripts do the same for unknown options, stray positionals, `--count -3`, and unusable database paths (generate-certificates.js and init-db.js without --reset), because parseArgs and openInitializedDatabase are called outside any try/catch. Exit codes are still 1; only the presentation is affected. The start-up test "invalid settings and unusable database files are reported the same way" covers PORT and a corrupt file only.
findings.expected: The same one-line message and exit code 1 that PORT and database problems get; a usage line for bad CLI arguments.
findings.reproduction:
In backend/ of my copy:
DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS=abc PORT=5503 DB_PATH=<scratch>/x1.sqlite node src/server.js -> "file:///.../src/db/sqlite.js:27  throw new Error(`DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS must be an integer ...`)" followed by "    at lockWaitFromEnv ..." lines, exit 1
SQLITE_DRIVER=bogus PORT=5503 DB_PATH=<scratch>/x1.sqlite node src/server.js -> "Error: Unsupported SQLITE_DRIVER \"bogus\" ...    at resolveDriver (...sqlite.js:86:11)", exit 1
(for comparison: PORT=abc ... -> single line "PORT must be an integer between 0 and 65535 (got \"abc\")")
node scripts/generate-certificates.js --bogus -> "TypeError [ERR_PARSE_ARGS_UNKNOWN_OPTION]: Unknown option '--bogus'" with stack
node scripts/generate-certificates.js --db <scratch> --count 3 (a directory) -> "SqliteError: unable to open database file" with stack
node scripts/generate-certificates.js --db <scratch>/garbage.sqlite --count 3 (text file) -> "SqliteError: file is not a database" with stack
node scripts/init-db.js --db <scratch>/garbage.sqlite -> same stack trace (with --reset it prints the clean "Reset failed, nothing was changed" message)
node scripts/init-db.js --bogus -> ERR_PARSE_ARGS_UNKNOWN_OPTION with stack
findings.suggestedFix: Validate the two settings in loadConfig (or import db/sqlite.js dynamically inside the try block of server.js), and wrap parseArgs and openInitializedDatabase in the scripts in a try/catch that prints err.message plus usage.

findings.title: Two verification tests do not exercise what their titles and the README claim (export connection release; TransactionAbortedError handling)
findings.criterion: general (verification tests); README section 7 "Export without blocking"
findings.location: backend/test/scale.test.js:304-319; backend/test/unit.test.js:279-281; README.md:259 ("the snapshot and the connection are released (also tested)")
findings.description:
(1) "an abandoned download releases its snapshot and connection" checks only that the read snapshot is gone (via a checkpoint). The snapshot is released by the ROLLBACK inside streamCsvExport, so the test still passes when the export's dedicated connection is never closed. With `reader.close()` removed from app.js every export, finished or abandoned, would leak a SQLite connection, and the whole scale suite stays green. The README's "(also tested)" is therefore true for the snapshot only.
(2) "exposes TransactionAbortedError for fatal mid-transaction failures" asserts only that `new TransactionAbortedError(...) instanceof Error`. The behaviour it names is not exercised anywhere: converting a failed savepoint rollback into that error (db/sqlite.js:205-211) and failing the bulk issue instead of continuing outside a transaction (services/bulkIssue.js:181). Disabling either leaves unit and acceptance tests green.
The production code is correct in both places; only the safety net is missing. For contrast, six other mutations I tried in this area were each caught by a failing test.
findings.expected: A test that fails when the export connection is not closed (for example by counting open descriptors on the database file, or closing a spy reader), and a test that forces a savepoint rollback failure and asserts that the bulk issue is rejected with nothing written.
findings.reproduction:
In a throw-away copy of backend/ inside my private tree (script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/61a877e9-483e-575a-b7cf-c5b8e94decb9/scratchpad/audit2/backend-review-fuzz/work/mutate-tests.sh):
M4: in src/app.js replace the body of the `finally { reader.close(); }` block of exportChunks with nothing, then `node --test --test-concurrency=1 test/scale.test.js` -> "# pass 12 # fail 0".
M1: in src/db/sqlite.js replace `throw err instanceof TransactionAbortedError ? err : new TransactionAbortedError(err ?? rollbackError);` with `throw err;`, then `node --test --test-concurrency=1 test/unit.test.js test/acceptance.test.js` -> "# pass 93 # fail 0".
M2: in src/services/bulkIssue.js delete the line `if (err instanceof TransactionAbortedError) throw err;`, same command -> "# pass 93 # fail 0".
Control: removing the busy_timeout restore in writeTransaction -> "# pass 92 # fail 1".
findings.suggestedFix: In the abandoned-download test also assert the server's descriptor count on the database file (or inject an openReader spy through createApp) returns to baseline; add a unit test that makes ROLLBACK TO fail (for example by issuing ROLLBACK inside the nested callback) and expects TransactionAbortedError, plus a bulk-issue test using the beforeIssue hook to do the same and expecting a failed request with no rows written.

findings.title: `npm start` fails on a fresh checkout when NODE_ENV=production is set in the shell
findings.description: The start script runs a plain `npm install` and then `vite build`, but vite and @vitejs/plugin-react are devDependencies of the frontend workspace. With NODE_ENV=production in the environment (common in container images and CI shells), npm omits devDependencies: 105 packages are installed instead of 122 and the build step dies with `sh: 1: vite: not found`. The app never starts, and the README troubleshooting section does not mention it. In an already working checkout the same `npm install` would also prune vite.
findings.expected: Spec section 1: "Provide one documented command that installs/uses declared dependencies, initializes demo data, and starts the full app." The command should not depend on NODE_ENV being unset.
findings.reproduction:
Fresh copy without node_modules, frontend/dist or data/*.sqlite*, Node 22.23.5:
  NODE_ENV=production PORT=5706 npm start
Observed:
  added 105 packages in 729ms
  > @cert-admin/frontend@1.0.0 build
  > vite build
  sh: 1: vite: not found
  npm error Lifecycle script `build` failed with error:
  npm error code 127
  exit=127
Nothing listens on the port. The same copy without NODE_ENV starts normally (122 packages).
findings.suggestedFix: Use `npm install --include=dev --no-audit --no-fund` in the start and test scripts, or move vite and @vitejs/plugin-react to `dependencies` of the frontend workspace.

findings.title: The generator permanently changes the quick-start East tenant row (serial counter); `--clear` does not restore it
findings.description: By default `npm run generate:east` writes into the default database data/cert-admin.sqlite. The seeded courses, learners, enrollments, certificates and audit events stay byte-identical (verified by per-table hashes), but the seeded tenant row is modified: `tenants.last_serial` for East goes from 7 to 100007. `npm run generate:east -- --clear` removes the generated rows but leaves the counter, so the quick-start scenario no longer behaves as documented: the README's bulk-issue example (`"serialNumber": "EAST-0000008"`) now yields EAST-0100008 and EAST-0100009. Only `npm run db:reset` gets back to the pristine dataset. While the rows are present, East's course list also grows from 3 to 13 courses. The README documents the counter ("only East's serial-number counter advances"), so this is a documented decision, but it conflicts with a literal reading of the spec.
findings.expected: Spec section 2: "Provide a separate CLI command or script to generate 100,000 certificate rows for one tenant (`East`) without altering the default quick-start dataset." Read strictly, the dataset produced by the quick start, including the East tenant row, must be the same after generating, or at least after `--clear`.
findings.location: /home/user/cert-admin-console/backend/src/db/generate.js (reserveSerials on the tenant row; deleteGenerated does not restore last_serial); /home/user/cert-admin-console/README.md section 4
findings.reproduction:
In my copy:
  node backend/scripts/init-db.js --db gen2.sqlite          -> tenants: ('East', 7), ('West', 4)
  npm run generate:east -- --db gen2.sqlite                 -> 100,007 certificates
  GET /api/courses as alice (server on that file)           -> 13 courses, 10 of them '... (load test)'
  npm run generate:east -- --db gen2.sqlite --clear         -> 'Removed 100,000 generated certificates'
  SELECT name,last_serial FROM tenants                      -> ('East', 100007), ('West', 4)
  POST /api/bulk-issues {"courseId":1}, Idempotency-Key demo-1
     -> issued: Marcus O'Connor id 12 EAST-0100008, Priya Sharma id 13 EAST-0100009
The README example for the same request on default data shows EAST-0000008. The same happened on the default database path in the fresh copy (the tenants_serial hash differed after generate + --clear; every other seeded table was identical).
findings.suggestedFix: Give generated certificates their own serial range (for example an `EAST-LT-` prefix, or a separate counter) so the tenant row is never touched, or have `--clear` restore last_serial to the highest non-generated serial. Alternatively make the generator write to a separate database file by default.

findings.title: npm warnings on every start and test run, including an install-scripts warning on Node 24
findings.description: On Node 24.22.3 (npm 11.19.1), which the README lists as verified, every `npm start` and `npm test` prints a four-line warning that better-sqlite3's install script is "not yet covered by allowScripts". A first-time evaluator cannot tell whether the native module was built (it was, in this run). A fresh install on any Node version also prints `npm warn deprecated prebuild-install@7.1.3`. Neither is mentioned in the README.
findings.expected: A quiet first run, or a line in the README troubleshooting section saying these warnings are harmless.
findings.reproduction:
Fresh copy, PATH=/opt/node24/bin:$PATH, `PORT=5704 npm start`:
  npm warn deprecated prebuild-install@7.1.3: No longer maintained. ...
  added 122 packages in 1s
  npm warn install-scripts 1 package has install scripts not yet covered by allowScripts:
  npm warn install-scripts   better-sqlite3@12.11.1 (install: prebuild-install || node-gyp rebuild --release)
  npm warn install-scripts Run `npm install-scripts ls` to review, or `npm install-scripts approve <pkg>` to allow.
The same warning block appears at the top of `npm test` output on Node 24. The server then started with (better-sqlite3) and the suite passed 105/105.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a troubleshooting line for the warnings, or declare the script as allowed for npm 11.

findings.title: Invalid DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS or SQLITE_DRIVER crashes with a raw stack trace
findings.description: PORT is validated in loadConfig and reported in one line. DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS and SQLITE_DRIVER are validated at module load in db/sqlite.js, outside server.js's try/catch, so a bad value produces an uncaught exception with a Node stack trace. server.js states the intent as "say what is wrong in one line, without a stack trace". The message text itself is clear.
findings.expected: The same one-line start-up error as for an invalid PORT.
findings.reproduction:
In my copy:
  DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS=abc PORT=5702 node backend/src/server.js
  -> file:///.../backend/src/db/sqlite.js:27
       throw new Error(`DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS must be an integer between 0 and 600000 milliseconds (got "${raw}")`);
     Error: DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS must be an integer ... (got "abc")
         at lockWaitFromEnv (...sqlite.js:27:11)   exit=1
Same for -1, 1.5 and 700000, and for SQLITE_DRIVER=foo (stack trace from resolveDriver).
For comparison, `PORT=abc node backend/src/server.js` prints only: PORT must be an integer between 0 and 65535 (got "abc").
findings.suggestedFix: Read these settings in loadConfig, or import the database module dynamically inside server.js's try/catch, so the error goes through exitWith().

findings.title: Node 20 has no fallback when the native SQLite module is missing, and the Node version statements disagree
findings.description: The README says "Node.js 20.19+, 22.12+ or 24+ with npm. Nothing else to install". On Node 20, and on 22.12 which predates unflagged node:sqlite, the app only works if better-sqlite3's install step succeeds. That needs either a prebuilt binary download from GitHub or a C++ toolchain. In this sandbox the Node 20 prebuilt was not available, so the first `npm start` compiled from source and took 75.7 s, against 2-3 s on Node 22 and 24. Without the module, Node 20 cannot start at all, and the troubleshooting entry only covers Node >= 22.13. Separately, three version statements disagree: the README says "24+", scripts/preflight.mjs accepts 23, and package.json engines `>=20.19.0` admits 21.x and 22.0-22.11, which the preflight rejects.
findings.expected: State in the README that on Node 20.x and 22.12 a working better-sqlite3 install is required, and make engines match the preflight (for example `^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0`).
findings.reproduction:
1) Fresh copy on Node 20.20.2: `PORT=5703 npm start` printed 'added 122 packages in 1m', was ready after 75.7 s, and node_modules/better-sqlite3/build contained Makefile, obj.target and sqlite3.a (a node-gyp build, not a prebuilt binary).
2) My copy with node_modules/better-sqlite3 moved away, Node 20.20.2: `PORT=5702 node backend/src/server.js` ->
   Error: No SQLite driver could be loaded. Use Node.js >= 22.13 (built-in node:sqlite) or make sure the optional "better-sqlite3" dependency installed correctly.
     - better-sqlite3: Cannot find package 'better-sqlite3' ...
     - node:sqlite: No such built-in module: node:sqlite     exit=1
   The same copy on Node 22.23.5 starts with '(node:sqlite)'.
3) Preflight with a simulated process.versions.node: 21.7.3 and 22.11.0 are rejected, 23.1.0 is accepted.
findings.suggestedFix: Add the Node 20 / 22.12 caveat to the troubleshooting entry and align engines, preflight and README.

findings.title: Several documented commands use POSIX-shell syntax with no Windows form
findings.description: Only the PORT override has a PowerShell form (`$env:PORT=4000; npm start`). The other documented commands assume a POSIX shell: `DB_PATH=/tmp/load.sqlite npm start`, `DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS=60000 npm start`, `HOST=127.0.0.1`, the `/tmp/load.sqlite` path, and the curl block (`A='...'; B='...'; URL=...`, `"$A"`, backslash line continuations, single-quoted JSON bodies). None of these run as written in cmd.exe or PowerShell. The npm scripts themselves contain nothing shell-specific (`&&` only, node entry points, no inline environment assignments), and the lockfile includes the darwin and win32 native packages, so `npm start`, `npm test`, `npm run generate:east` and `npm run db:reset` look portable.
findings.expected: A one-line note that the examples assume bash (Git Bash or WSL on Windows), or PowerShell equivalents for the other variables.
findings.location: /home/user/cert-admin-console/README.md (commands table in section 1, section 4 code block, section 5 curl block, section 9 troubleshooting)
findings.reproduction: Static review of README.md and the three package.json files; no Windows or macOS machine was available, so nothing was executed there.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a short note on Windows usage next to the existing PowerShell hint.

result.summary: I audited backend/test as evidence for A1-A7: 11 full-suite runs under varied conditions, every test run in isolation, and 134 distinct single-change mutants of the backend. The suite is stable (105/105 in every run, no flaky failure in about 170 runs) and catches every direct violation of A1, A3, A4, A5 and A7 that I injected. It does not catch a bulk issue made non-atomic, removal of the per-learner savepoint, or a tenant override through a request parameter on the detail endpoint. 31 mutants survive; 19 of those are real defects, each of which one of my 12 added kill tests detects. No acceptance criterion fails in the delivered code; every finding concerns the quality of the test evidence.
checksPerformed: Baseline: the backend test command (unit + acceptance + scale, --test-concurrency=1) passed 105/105 in 11 full runs of a private copy: 3 plain runs (27-31 s), TZ=America/New_York, TZ=Pacific/Kiritimati, TZ=Australia/Sydney, SQLITE_DRIVER=node (confirmed driverName is node:sqlite), wall clock shifted to early 2025 and to 2031 via a Date preload in runner and child processes, the three files in parallel (default runner concurrency), and once with 3 busy-loop processes running. No failure in any of them.

Documented command: `npm test` at the root of a private copy exited 0 with 105 tests / 105 pass in 27 s (README says 105 tests, about 30 s). data/ still held only .gitkeep and TMPDIR held no test directories afterwards.
Leftovers after normal runs: none. After each of the 11 runs TMPDIR was empty of cert-admin-* directories and no node process with cwd in my copy remained.

Isolation: each of the 105 leaf tests run alone with --test-name-pattern (33 unit, 60 acceptance, 12 scale): 100 pass, 5 fail because they need state from an earlier test in the same suite. Each of the 11 acceptance suites run alone passes, so the suite-level independence claimed in the file header holds.

Mutation testing: 134 distinct single-purpose mutants applied one at a time to backend/src in a private copy, unit+acceptance run first and scale run for anything that survived, sources restored and diffed against the original after every mutant. 103 killed, 31 survived.

A1 mutants (16): tenant predicate removed from list rows, list count, export, detail, revoke, audit list, findCourse, listCourses, getBulkOperation, listBulkOperations, global key lookup, and a tenantId query override on the list endpoint were all killed. Survivors: tenantId override on detail, tenantId override in the bulk-issue body, key lookup tenant-wide instead of per admin, and roster join without tenant (equivalent, the course is already tenant-checked).

A2 mutants (14): no key check under the lock, no fast-path check, replay with different body, replay with status 200, key not stored, deferred BEGIN, sleeping inside SQLite, certificate UNIQUE backstop removed, issue audit skipped, issue audit duplicated were all killed. Survivors: key claimed in a separate committed transaction, per-learner savepoint removed, case-insensitive key match, and a non-unique idempotency index (equivalent while the code is correct).

A3 mutants (8): mismatch ignored, unreadable body not treated as a mismatch, fingerprint over courseId only, fingerprint ignoring the body, key-order-sensitive fingerprint, 409 that overwrites the stored hash, unreadable body skipping the key check, and an under-lock check that replays on mismatch were killed. The one survivor compares only the first hex digit of the hash and passes because none of the suite's sample payloads happen to collide; I do not count it as a gap.

A4 mutants (9): revoked branch removed, revoked certificate re-issued, incomplete learners issued, in-progress treated as completed, already-certified check dropped, roster join ignoring the course, one failure failing the whole request, failed reported as skipped, missing skip reason. All 9 killed.

A5 mutants (14): sort by UTC date, local date stored as UTC date, local date computed in Sydney for every tenant, export formatted in UTC, export printing the raw instant, midnight as 24, fixed Sydney offset without DST, wrong zone in list / export / detail, swapped seed zones, sort by id only, broken formatter cache were killed; `issued` ordering without the instant was killed only by the scale test. Sorting by instant then id survives and is equivalent, because the local date is monotonic in the instant.

A6 mutants (27): order direction ignored, wrong sort column, tie-break always ascending, random tie-break (course, learner, issued; the latter two killed only by scale), export ignoring search / status / sort / direction, 50,000-row limit, swapped columns, dropped last batch, missing header zone, CSV quoting bugs, export on the main connection, generator off by one, generator without ties, generator altering seed rows were killed. Survivors: ORDER BY without the id tie-breaker (three variants), no INDEXED BY hint, both together, tie-break by serial, no explicit BEGIN around the export (all equivalent in practice) and export connection never closed (real).

Tie-breaker probe: on a 100,007-row database with the 'no index hint and no id tie-breaker' mutant I exported 210 combinations of sort x order x status x search twice each and compared against the database. No pair of exports differed and no sort-key violation occurred. The only deviation was sort=status&order=desc with a status filter (11 combinations), where ties came back in ascending instead of descending id. SQLite index entries end in the rowid, so omitting the explicit tie-breaker is not observable as non-determinism; A6 determinism holds either way.

A7 mutants (8): no status guard on the revoke UPDATE, fast path removed, both removed, audit skipped, audit duplicated, audit written when nothing changed, alreadyRevoked always false, status not changed. All 8 killed; the guard removal and the audit-when-unchanged mutants were killed only by the two-server lock test.

List mutants (13): offset and limit off-by-one variants, LIKE not escaped, underscore not escaped, search ignoring serial or learner name, prefix-only search, status filter ignored, unfiltered total were killed. Survivors: totalPages wrong for exact multiples, backslash not escaped, search also matching course title.

Schema mutants (13): each composite (x, tenant_id) foreign key weakened to a single-column reference. 8 killed by unit tests; 5 survive unit, acceptance and scale (bulk_issue_operations.actor_admin_id and .course_id, certificates.issued_by_admin_id and .revoked_by_admin_id, audit_events.actor_admin_id).

Other mutants: generator deleting all audit events of the tenant and generator editing a seed certificate were killed. Survivors: bulk result issuedLocal in UTC, revokedLocal in UTC, audit createdLocal in UTC, generator bumping West's serial counter, and export batches of 20,000 rows (a tuning change, not a defect).

Kill tests: I wrote 12 tests (K1-K12) in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/61a877e9-483e-575a-b7cf-c5b8e94decb9/scratchpad/audit2/test-suite-quality/kill/audit-kill.test.js and audit-kill2.test.js. All 12 pass on the delivered code, and each of the 19 real-defect survivors fails at least one of them.

Race coverage: re-ran the 'no key check under the lock' mutant 5 more times against acceptance.test.js. In all 6 runs only the two forced-overlap lock tests failed; '25 simultaneous requests', 'holds across processes' and the other unforced concurrency tests passed every time.

Blocking-export margin: re-ran the single-blocking-batch export mutant 5 more times against scale.test.js. Killed 6/6, each time only by the `latencies.length >= 3` assertion (observed 1, 2, 1, 1, 1, 2); the slowest list request was 617-956 ms against a 2,000 ms bound.

Connection-leak probe: server on port 5802, 300 small exports. Delivered code: 25 fds before, 26 after 100, 200 and 300 exports. With the never-closed mutant: 103 after 100, 165 after 200, 138 after 300 (garbage collection reclaims some).

Memory probe for the snapshot assertion: assert.deepEqual with a one-sided difference of 500 learner rows peaked at 176 MB RSS, with 2,000 rows at 2,039 MB (quadratic). Both scale runs of the 'generated learners not flagged' mutant ended with the test file process dying without output while the kernel reported an out-of-memory kill.

Interrupted runs: SIGTERM to the runner and SIGINT to the process group left no server process but left the cert-admin-test-* temp directory; SIGKILL of the runner left one orphaned `node src/server.js` (ppid 1) plus the temp directory. I killed the orphan myself.
Environment sensitivity: with HOST=0.0.0.0 or HOST=<this machine's hostname> the 'actor context' suite passes; with HOST=127.0.0.2 all 3 of its tests fail with 'fetch failed'.

Flakiness: across about 170 suite or file runs (baseline, isolation, mutants, repeats, under load) every failure of a timing-sensitive test was explained by the mutation under test. No unexplained failure occurred.

Machine time zone and date: grep of backend/src and backend/test found no local-time accessors (getHours, toLocale*String without locale, getTimezoneOffset); the three TZ runs and the two shifted-clock runs confirm independence.
Frontend: frontend/ contains no test files and no test tooling (package.json has only dev, build, preview); the backend test script lists only the three backend files.

Cleanup: every process I started is stopped, no listener remains on ports 5800-5849, all three private copies have pristine src and test directories, and nothing was written under /home/user/cert-admin-console.

findings.title: A bulk issue made non-atomic (idempotency record committed before the certificates) passes all 105 tests
findings.description: The README and the comment at the top of bulkIssue.js say the whole operation is one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction and that a crash before COMMIT leaves no certificates, no audit events and no key. No test makes an operation fail after it has started: every rejection the suite exercises (400, 404, 409, 413, 503) happens before the bulk_issue_operations row is inserted, and the only injected failure is per-learner and caught. A mutant that commits the operation row (key, hash, status 'running', response NULL) in one transaction and does the issuing in a second one therefore survives. With that mutant any failure between the two commits burns the key, and a concurrent identical request from another process can read a record with no response.
findings.expected: A test in which the operation fails as a whole after it has begun, asserting that nothing is stored (no certificate, audit event or operation row) and that a retry with the same key is the first execution.
findings.suggestedFix: Add K2 (or an equivalent using the injectable `now` throwing at completion) to the A2 suite.

findings.title: The 'leaves no partial writes' test passes with the per-learner savepoint removed
findings.description: README section 6 credits the 'simulated failure' test with verifying that each learner is issued inside a savepoint. The test's hook throws before issueCertificate has written anything, so there is nothing to roll back; the assertion commented 'The failed attempt did not consume a serial number either' holds with or without the savepoint. Without the savepoint, a learner whose issue fails after the certificate INSERT (for example on the audit insert) would keep a certificate with no audit event while being reported as failed.
findings.expected: The simulated failure should happen after at least one write of the failing learner, so that the rollback is what the assertions observe.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the hook write before throwing, as in K1, or add an afterInsert seam and fail there.

findings.title: The in-process 'concurrent' tests never overlap; race protection is exercised only by the two-server lock tests
findings.description: Connection.writeTransaction runs synchronously from BEGIN IMMEDIATE to COMMIT whenever the lock is free, so N requests sent to one server are handled strictly one after another. As a result '25 simultaneous requests are one logical operation', 'different keys racing', 'a concurrent pair with one key and two payloads' and 'concurrent revocations still produce a single audit event' pass with the race protections removed. 'holds across processes' (20 requests over two servers, no lock holder) also passed every time. The only tests that detect these mutants are the forced-overlap tests in 'A2 - while another process holds the database write lock', each with exactly two requests, one per server.
findings.reproduction:
Mutant A (bulkIssue.js, check under the lock removed):
-    const raced = answerFromStoredKey(db, actor, idempotencyKey, requestHash);
+    const raced = null;
Six runs of acceptance.test.js: 58/60 pass each time. The only failures were 'identical requests to two servers overlap for certain and still execute exactly once' and 'one key with two payloads on two servers'.

Mutant B (ledger.js revokeCertificate, status guard removed):
-      WHERE id = @certificateId AND tenant_id = @tenantId AND status = 'active'`,
+      WHERE id = @certificateId AND tenant_id = @tenantId`,
Only 'a new revocation waits for the lock, then takes effect once' fails; 'concurrent revocations still produce a single audit event' (12 parallel requests) passes.

Mutant C (ledger.js, line `if (changes !== 1) return false;` deleted): same single failing test.
findings.expected: Tests named for concurrency should fail when the protection against concurrent execution is removed, or be described as sequential-equivalent.
findings.suggestedFix: Extend the lock-holder technique: several identical requests per server (so that two wait inside one process) released together, for both bulk issue and revoke.

findings.title: A tenant taken from request parameters is only probed on list and export; a detail-endpoint override leaks East data to Bob and passes the suite
findings.description: The README states the tenant is never read from the URL, query string or body. The A1 list test sends tenant, tenantId and tenant_id and the export test sends tenant and tenantId, but the detail, bulk-issue and revoke tests never do. A route that honours ?tenantId= on the detail endpoint returns East's certificate to Bob with 200 and no test fails. The same override in the bulk-issue body also survives the suite; there the composite foreign keys stop the write, but the response is 500 instead of 404.
findings.expected: The parameter-override probes of the list test applied to detail, bulk issue and revoke as well.
findings.suggestedFix: Add K5; it is a few lines.

findings.title: Idempotency-key scoping is verified only across tenants: per-admin scope and exact key matching are untested
findings.description: The test 'idempotency keys are scoped to the actor' uses Alice and Bob, who are in different tenants, so a lookup scoped to the tenant alone is indistinguishable. No test uses two keys that differ only in letter case, so a case-insensitive lookup also survives; it would answer a new operation with 409 or with another operation's stored result. The seed has one admin per tenant, so the first point cannot occur with the demo data.
findings.reproduction:
Mutant 1 (bulkIssue.js answerFromStoredKey):
-      WHERE tenant_id = @tenantId AND actor_admin_id = @adminId AND idempotency_key = @idempotencyKey`,
+      WHERE tenant_id = @tenantId AND (actor_admin_id = @adminId OR 1) AND idempotency_key = @idempotencyKey ORDER BY id LIMIT 1`,
Mutant 2:
+      ... AND idempotency_key = @idempotencyKey COLLATE NOCASE`,
Both: unit + acceptance 93/93, scale 12/12.

Kill tests K3 (insert a second East admin carol@east.test; her request with Alice's key and body must be executed, not replayed) and K4 (Forklift with key 'Key-A', then First Aid with 'key-a' must be 201 and not replayed) in the same audit-kill.test.js pass on the delivered code and fail on the respective mutant.
findings.expected: Tests matching the README claim 'Idempotency keys are scoped to (tenant, admin)'.
findings.suggestedFix: Add K3 and K4.

findings.title: README says connection release after an abandoned export is 'also tested'; an export connection that is never closed passes the suite
findings.description: 'an abandoned download releases its snapshot and connection' checks only that WAL frames can be checkpointed, which proves the read snapshot is released. With reader.close() removed the snapshot is still released by the ROLLBACK, so the test passes while every export leaks a SQLite connection and its file descriptors until garbage collection happens to reclaim some.
findings.expected: A test that observes the connection itself, since README line 259 says the snapshot and the connection are released and that this is tested.
findings.suggestedFix: Add K6, or assert on the server's descriptor count before and after a batch of exports.

findings.title: The A6 non-blocking check catches a fully blocking export only through a count threshold with a margin of one
findings.description: 'list requests stay responsive while exports are streaming at full speed' has two assertions: at least 3 list requests answered while the three exports run, and slowest list request under 2,000 ms. With an export that builds the whole 100,000-row file in one synchronous batch, the slowest list request was 617-956 ms, so the time bound never triggers. The mutant is killed only because 1 or 2 list requests were counted instead of 3. A faster client or a slower body transfer would let a blocking export pass. A single export, the common case, is not measured at all.
findings.expected: A bound tied to the measured behaviour, for example slowest list request below a few hundred ms or below a fraction of the export duration, and a count proportional to export time.
findings.suggestedFix: Assert `worst < exportMs / 4` or a fixed bound near 250 ms, and require a count such as one list answer per 50 ms of export.

findings.description: The unit tests exercise the composite keys on enrollments (course, learner), certificates (course, learner, enrollment, bulk operation) and audit_events (certificate, bulk operation). The five that tie rows to an admin or tie a bulk operation to its course are not exercised. Kill test K10 in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/61a877e9-483e-575a-b7cf-c5b8e94decb9/scratchpad/audit2/test-suite-quality/kill/audit-kill2.test.js attempts the five cross-tenant writes and expects /FOREIGN KEY/; it passes on the delivered schema and fails on each of the five mutants.

findings.title: The 'quick-start dataset untouched' assertion exhausts memory instead of failing when the generator leaks many rows
findings.description: scale.test.js compares two snapshots with assert.deepEqual. When the generator puts its 10,000 learners into the non-generated set, Node's assertion diff needs memory quadratic in the size of the difference. The test file process does not report an assertion; it is killed by the kernel for lack of memory after about 28 s, the run shows only 'test/scale.test.js - test failed' with no subtest output, the 100k-row server it started is left running, and the kernel may pick an unrelated process as victim. The defect is still reported as a failure (exit code 1), but without a diagnostic and with collateral damage.
findings.reproduction:
Mutant (backend/src/db/generate.js):
-           VALUES (@tenantId, @name, @email, 1, @createdAt)`,
+           VALUES (@tenantId, @name, @email, 0, @createdAt)`,
`node --test --test-reporter=spec test/scale.test.js`, run twice: both ended after 28.4 s and 29.3 s with 'tests 1, pass 0, fail 1' and only '✖ test/scale.test.js ... test failed'. Both times the environment reported that the kernel killed a process for lack of memory, and one orphaned `node src/server.js` from the test remained (I killed it).

Mechanism, bounded: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/61a877e9-483e-575a-b7cf-c5b8e94decb9/scratchpad/audit2/test-suite-quality/tools/deepequal-mem.mjs runs assert.deepEqual on 13 versus N learner-like rows. 500 extra rows: 144 ms, 176 MB RSS. 2,000 extra rows: 1.9 s, 2,039 MB RSS. I did not run 10,000.
findings.expected: A bounded comparison that fails with a readable message, for example comparing row counts and ids first, or comparing JSON strings with assert.ok as the export tests already do.
findings.suggestedFix: Compare per-table counts and a hash or JSON string of each table before any deepEqual, and deepEqual only when sizes match.

findings.title: Five tests fail when run on their own because they rely on an earlier test in the same suite
findings.description: The file header promises independence between suites, which holds. Inside suites, five tests need state created by a preceding test, so they cannot be run individually (for example with --test-name-pattern or .only) and would produce follow-on failures if the earlier test failed.
findings.reproduction:
In a private copy's backend directory: `node --test --test-concurrency=1 --test-name-pattern '^<name>$' test/acceptance.test.js` for each test name. Failing alone:
- 'without a key a repeat is a new operation, but still cannot issue twice' (actual issued 2 / skipped 3, expected 0 / 5)
- 'same key with a changed payload is a 409 as well' (actual 201, expected 409)
- 'deeply nested JSON is a payload like any other, never a server error' (actual 201, expected 409)
- 'a later run finds nobody left to certify' (actual issued 2, expected 0)
- 'repeating the request is a no-op: same state, no second audit event' (alreadyRevoked actual false, expected true)
The other 100 tests pass alone; all 11 acceptance suites pass alone.
findings.expected: Each test sets up what it needs, or the dependency is stated.
findings.suggestedFix: Issue or revoke the prerequisite inside each of the five tests (the calls are idempotent).

findings.title: Test harness: interrupted runs leave temp databases, a killed runner leaves an orphaned server, and an inherited HOST variable breaks every HTTP test
findings.description: Normal runs clean up completely. When the run is interrupted, the cert-admin-test-* directory under the OS temp directory stays. If the runner is killed with SIGKILL (or by the kernel, as in the memory finding) the spawned `node src/server.js` survives with ppid 1, still listening on its port. Separately, serverEnv pins PORT, DB_PATH, LOG_REQUESTS and STATIC_DIR but not HOST, while startServer rewrites the URL to 127.0.0.1; a HOST exported in the developer's shell that names another address makes every server-based test fail.
findings.reproduction:
/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/61a877e9-483e-575a-b7cf-c5b8e94decb9/scratchpad/audit2/test-suite-quality/tools/interrupt.py starts `node --test ... test/acceptance.test.js` and signals it after 4 s:
- SIGTERM to the runner: 0 servers left, temp dir cert-admin-test-3FkVNB left
- SIGKILL to the runner: 1 server left (ppid=1), temp dir left
- SIGINT to the process group: 0 servers left, temp dir left

`HOST=127.0.0.2 node --test --test-concurrency=1 --test-name-pattern '^actor context$' test/acceptance.test.js` gives tests 3, pass 0, fail 3 ('TypeError: fetch failed'); with HOST=0.0.0.0 or HOST=vm (resolves to 127.0.0.1 here) it gives 3/3.
findings.expected: The harness sets HOST itself, and servers do not outlive the test process.
findings.suggestedFix: Add HOST: '127.0.0.1' to serverEnv; have the spawned server exit when its stdin closes (pass a pipe) or register a process 'exit' handler that kills children and removes the temp directories.

findings.title: No automated test touches the frontend, so the UI requirements of the core workflows have no test evidence
findings.description: `npm test` runs only backend/test. The spec's workflow requirements that live in the UI are therefore unverified by the suite: preventing duplicate bulk-issue submissions and showing operation status, repeating a lost request with the same Idempotency-Key ('Retry safely'), the revoke confirmation, the export link carrying the active search and sort, and the loading, empty and error states. The README is accurate about this (it describes the tests as black-box over HTTP against the server), and the spec makes the test command optional, so this is a coverage gap and not a false claim.
findings.reproduction: In the deliverable: `find frontend -name '*.test.*' -o -name '*.spec.*'` (outside node_modules) returns nothing; frontend/package.json has only the scripts dev, build and preview and no test dependency; backend/package.json's test script is `node --test ... test/unit.test.js test/acceptance.test.js test/scale.test.js`. The Idempotency-Key the UI sends is generated in frontend/src/components/BulkIssuePage.jsx:11 and sent in frontend/src/api.js:97-102, and neither file is referenced by any test.
findings.expected: At least a smoke test of the bulk-issue page (button locked while in flight, same key on retry) and of the export link, since A2 depends on the client reusing its key.
findings.suggestedFix: A small Playwright test against the built app covering double-click on Issue, Retry safely after a forced 5xx, and the export URL after a search and sort.
